items.body: Test Dept and the Welsh performance company Brith Gof release “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” on 4 December 2026 via Artoffact Records. The set expands their 1989 album into a 3CD/1DVD box, alongside a separate red vinyl LP and a digital edition. “Gododdin” is based on Y Gododdin, the earliest surviving Welsh-language poem, written around 600 AD. It tells of 300 Celtic warriors who attacked 100,000 invading Angles and lost. Test Dept and Brith Gof first staged the piece as a live performance at an abandoned Rover car factory in Cardiff in December 1988, using 600 tons of sand, 50 trees and 30 wrecked cars on a set that flooded as the show went on. Further performances followed in 1989 in Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland. The original 1989 studio album was produced by Ken Thomas at Jacobs Studios from Test Dept’s existing studio and field recordings, augmented with brass and wind courtesy of Brith Gof’s John E R Hardy and bagpipes from Alistair Adams. Paul Jamrozy’s voice runs alongside the Welsh-language vocals of Lis Hughes Jones. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” widens that original 7-track album with 19 tracks that have not previously been released. The first disc is a reworked version built from newly unearthed multitrack tapes of the early studio sessions, put together by Test Dept founder members Graham Cunnington and Paul Jamrozy during the summer of 2026. The second disc carries a live recording from one of the 1989 performances, staged in a quarry in Polverigi, Italy. The DVD holds a documentary from the period, with live footage and interviews with performers, academics and other experts. Compiled by Test Dept with input from Brith Gof members Lis Hughes Jones, John E R Hardy and Heike Roms, the set was remastered by Paul Lavigne at Kontrast Mastering. It comes in a 5-panel ecopak with a 24-page booklet of archival imagery and writing, including an essay by author and Test Dept researcher Alexei Monroe. The artwork for both the box and the separate red vinyl LP was redesigned by Paul Jamrozy and Stefan Alt (ant-zen); the vinyl edition carries the original album plus one previously unreleased track and a printed insert. Ahead of the box set, Test Dept released the advance single “Gwr a Aeth Gatraeth / Prologue (Early Studio Sessions, Reworked 2026)” on 2 October 2026, available on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” is the second in Test Dept’s ongoing series of archival reissues on Artoffact Records, who signed the band in 2025 for catalogue reissues and a new album. It follows the 4xCD “Industrial Overture: Studio & Live Recordings 1982-1985”, released a year earlier. Artoffact will also release new Test Dept material in 2027. A separate event ties into the reissue: Test Dept and Brith Gof take part in a discussion and Q&A about “Gododdin” at Chapter in Cardiff on 24 October, as part of the Experimentica festival’s 25th-anniversary programme. About Test Dept Test Dept formed in London in the early 1980s as an industrial music group built around live percussion on scrap metal and found objects. In 1988 and 1989, the band collaborated with the Welsh avant-garde theatre company Brith Gof on “Gododdin”, staging it first at an abandoned car factory in Cardiff and then on tour in Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland. The 1989 studio album version was produced by Ken Thomas at Jacobs Studios. Test Dept returned to active release and performance in the 2020s. In 2025, the band signed to Artoffact Records for a series of catalogue reissues alongside a new studio album. The first of those reissues, the 4xCD “Industrial Overture: Studio & Live Recordings 1982-1985”, arrived in October 2025. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster”, out 4 December 2026, is the second. Current members Graham Cunnington and Paul Jamrozy built new versions of the early “Gododdin” studio sessions for the reissue during the summer of 2026, working from recently unearthed multitrack tapes. Test Dept continue to tour, with confirmed UK and European dates running from October 2026 into the summer of 2027, and have a new studio album due via Artoffact in 2027. About Brith Gof Brith Gof is a Welsh performance company known for large-scale, site-specific theatre work that drew on Welsh history and language. Co-founded by figures including Mike Pearson, Lis Hughes Jones and Clifford McLucas, the company staged “Gododdin” with Test Dept in Cardiff in 1988, adapting the early Welsh poem Y Gododdin into a promenade performance inside a disused car factory. Hughes Jones, John E R Hardy and Heike Roms were directly involved in compiling “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” alongside Test Dept.

items.excerpt: On 1 October 2026, Nachtmahr chose Poland to open the longest and largest tour in the project’s history: three consecutive club dates in Wrocław, Poznań and Warsaw, with Cygnosic and Bagger 258 joining the opening run before IMPERIVM continues further across Europe. A new programme
items.body: On 1 October 2026, Nachtmahr chose Poland to open the longest and largest tour in the project’s history: three consecutive club dates in Wrocław, Poznań and Warsaw, with Cygnosic and Bagger 258 joining the opening run before IMPERIVM continues further across Europe. When Thomas Rainer and I spoke ahead of the tour, he admitted that beginning in Poland had originally been a logistical decision, but previous experience with Polish audiences made it an unexpectedly appropriate one. A new programme inevitably introduces a degree of uncertainty, and he expected the energy of the Polish crowd to remove it very quickly. Wrocław supplied a fairly emphatic confirmation. Three bands approached electronic physicality from markedly different directions, yet there was no weak transition between them. Bagger 258 worked through blunt rhythmic force, aggressive vocals and a very direct relationship with the dancefloor; Cygnosic loosened that geometry into something darker, broader and more fluid; Nachtmahr then inherited a room already fully activated and pushed it into a much less orderly state. The evening did not feel like a headliner plus obligatory support. Its construction mattered. And Wrocław really is being spoiled this autumn. The number of strong dark-electronic, industrial and gothic concerts passing through the city has reached the point where they are beginning to form a genuine season rather than a handful of unrelated bookings. This was another very persuasive addition. Bagger 258 Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil I should already have seen Bagger 258 at the NCN Warm-Up this year, but unfortunately missed them there, so Wrocław finally gave me the chance to catch up. It took very little time to understand what I had missed. The Augsburg duo, Nico von der Eisenmühle and Tim “Hacke” Schmelzer, released their debut album “Aufwärts gehts bergab” in February 2026. Its language places them firmly inside EBM: Arbeiterwut, Funktion, Kontrolle!, Werkshalle 4, “Körperkommando“, Schicht im Schacht. Machinery, work, discipline and repetitive physical action are everywhere in the imagery, while Nachtmahr themselves contributed a remix of “Werkshalle 4” to the record. Live, however, Bagger 258 were far more interesting than a catalogue of genre references might suggest. Their greatest strength was immediacy. The beats came down hard and square, the vocals had real abrasion to them, and yet the performance never became rigid. There was too much visible enjoyment onstage for that. The music was aggressive, but the aggression kept converting itself into movement. There is a considerable difference between performing the visual grammar of old-school EBM and actually making a room respond to it. Bagger 258 did the latter. The pulse was almost mechanically regular, but the communication around it was human, animated and frequently playful. They were not protecting a historical form. They were using it. For an opening band, they also did exactly what an opening band should do without ever seeming subordinate to what followed. The audience did not require a long negotiation before deciding whether it was ready to move. Bagger 258 established that physical vocabulary almost immediately, and by the end of the set the room had already shifted from people waiting for the main act into people actively participating in the evening. Rainer had told me before the tour that the right support band changes the condition in which a headliner encounters its audience. If someone else has already brought the room to a certain level, you do not have to begin from zero. Bagger 258 made the point rather convincingly. Absolute knockout. Cygnosic Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Cygnosic changed the type of pressure rather than reducing it. The Athens project of Georgios Psaroudakis has a long history within dark electro, with Psaroudakis writing, performing and producing the material himself. “Demystify”, released in 2023, was Cygnosic’s seventh full-length album, while 2025’s “Theorem” reconstructed existing Cygnosic pieces through metal arrangements and showed how naturally heavier structures can sit inside the project’s electronic identity. That breadth could be felt live. Compared with the harder edges of Bagger 258, Cygnosic sounded more fluid and spacious, but describing it simply as “gentler” would undersell what was happening. The force had merely changed direction. Instead of striking repeatedly at the centre, the arrangements seemed to spread across the room, gathering weight through layers, melody and continuity. There was more air inside the music and more room for individual elements to develop. The rhythms still carried the performance, but the relationship between rhythm and atmosphere was different. Movement became less regimented, more continuous. The set could be forceful without constantly attacking. That made Cygnosic particularly effective in the middle position. Bagger 258 had already established the body as the evening’s main point of communication; Cygnosic kept the body engaged while changing how it moved. The result was dynamic, dark and surprisingly graceful. It also prevented the three-band bill from becoming three variations on the same impact. By the time Cygnosic finished, the audience was still physically engaged but had travelled through a noticeably different emotional texture, leaving Nachtmahr with exactly the kind of room Thomas Rainer had spoken about before the tour: warmed up, responsive and ready to be pushed considerably further. Nachtmahr Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil When Thomas Rainer and I spoke for Side-Line in August, much of our conversation circled around a contradiction at the centre of Nachtmahr live. The project’s visual language is built from command, discipline, uniforms, hierarchy, severity and theatricalised authority. Producing that world requires enormous control: sound, lighting, costumes, movement, timing and musicianship all have to function together. Yet the result Nachtmahr seeks from the audience is almost the exact opposite. The crowd is invited to abandon restraint, surrender to rhythm and lose control inside something that has been very carefully controlled on its behalf. For Rainer, the construction starts with the songs themselves. As he told me then, “The setlist is the script for the movie we present every night on tour.” The first IMPERIVM show gave that sentence a much more concrete meaning. The album, released on 26 June 2026 through Trisol, develops methods Rainer had already begun testing on “Verboten!” rather than simply applying another layer of production to an established Nachtmahr template. In our interview, he described Verboten! not as the end point of an evolution but as the record that established the method for what followed. IMPERIVM takes that logic further while retaining the project’s unmistakable rhythmic and visual identity. Onstage, however, theory disappears very quickly behind physical action. Thomas Rainer commands a room in a way relatively few performers can. That is not simply another way of saying that he is charismatic. What impressed me was how actively he reads the response in front of him. A gesture produces a reaction; he catches that reaction and sends it back, larger. The next rhythmic hit strengthens it again. The relationship becomes circular rather than one-directional. In Wrocław, that feedback loop escalated with remarkable speed. The entire live formation is central to why it works. Nachtmahr no longer reads as one central figure surrounded by secondary decoration. There are several simultaneous points of attention across the stage, and the movement between them gives the performance much of its tension. The musicians maintain the structural discipline, while the women in the production are integral to the stage language rather than simply ornamental additions. Their choreography, posture and interaction reinforce Nachtmahr’s play with authority and submission. They contribute to the sense of order, but also to its deliberate instability. The more precisely the stage is arranged, the more excessive the activity in front of it can become. And the audience went completely wild. Not “wild” merely because people were dancing hard. What happened was cumulative. The room became denser at the front, hands were constantly raised, bodies moved forward, and the separation between active participants and passive spectators progressively disappeared. Every successful exchange with the stage seemed to authorise a larger response. That is why “madness” is both tempting and slightly inadequate as a description. The apparent madness had an architecture. It was being built. Rainer had explained in our interview that his band and crew remove much of the need for conscious control once he is onstage, allowing him to respond instinctively and become absorbed in the energy coming back from the room. He wanted the same for the audience: a framework reliable enough that people could safely lose themselves inside it. “I have a wonderful band and crew who take the need for control out of my hands, so I can completely let go onstage and simply become one with the energy of the crowd.” Wrocław demonstrated exactly what he meant. Bagger 258 and Cygnosic had already brought the audience a considerable distance. Nachtmahr did not have to spend the opening part of the set manufacturing involvement. They could begin by directing something already in motion. From there, the room became increasingly feral. One of the most striking aspects of a Nachtmahr show remains this gap between what the imagery appears to promise and what the live experience actually produces. Onstage there is hierarchy, command and discipline; in front of it, the effect is strangely collective. The imagery separates roles, while the music dissolves them. People move together. The stricter the construction onstage became, the less restrained the audience appeared. And in the middle of all that force came one of the evening’s most delicate moments. Thomas Rainer took time to remember Witek Kopytko, our colleague and a deeply valued member of the scene, who passed away earlier this year. He distributed tiny toy horses among people in the audience in Witek’s memory. It was a small, personal gesture, but precisely because nothing about it was inflated into spectacle, it carried real emotional weight. For those of us who knew Witek, worked alongside him or simply shared this scene with him over the years, the moment briefly changed the emotional temperature of the room. The concert had been built around movement, control and physical intensity; suddenly there was space for affection and remembrance. It was a genuinely beautiful tribute to a colleague who is very much missed. It also said something important about what these scenes actually consist of. Bands, promoters, journalists, photographers and audiences may occupy different roles at an event, but over years those roles begin to overlap into a community. Remembering one of its people in the middle of such a large production was not a detour from the evening. It belonged there. When the music resumed, the contrast only made the final part of the set more pronounced. The machinery returned, the crowd returned to movement, but the evening had briefly revealed something much softer underneath it. The setlist Rainer’s description of the setlist as dramaturgy becomes particularly interesting when looking at the stage sheet from Wrocław. New IMPERIVM material was not placed into an isolated promotional block; it sat among songs from different periods of Nachtmahr’s catalogue. With the clearly crossed-out alternatives on the photographed sheet omitted, the visible running order was: Wer Wind sät, Keine Lieder, Weil ich’s kann!, Liebst du mich?, Tanzdiktator, Stärker als ihr Hass, Sirenen, Heile mich, Die Straße, Kampfbereit, Beweg dich!, “Mädchen in Uniform“, Unterwerfung, Der Schlaf, Katharsis. Ending on “Katharsis” was especially fitting. By that stage, the idea had already been enacted physically for well over an hour. Wrocław, and what comes next There was something especially satisfying about watching all of this happen here. Wrocław has been remarkably well served by dark music this autumn, and the concentration of good bookings is beginning to change the rhythm of the city’s scene. It matters that international industrial, EBM, darkwave and gothic artists are not simply appearing as occasional exceptions but arriving regularly enough for audiences to develop continuity between events. That continuity is important because nights like this depend on difference as much as similarity. Bagger 258 took familiar EBM mechanics and made them feel immediate, aggressive and highly physical rather than nostalgic. Cygnosic widened that physicality into something more fluid, melodic and atmospheric. Nachtmahr then absorbed everything accumulated during the previous sets and used it as raw material for a performance based on reciprocal escalation. The Polish IMPERIVM opening continues with Poznań at Pod Minogą on 2 October and Warsaw at VooDoo Club on 3 October, before the tour moves on internationally. Audience in Wrocław Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil About Nachtmahr, Cygnosic and Bagger 258 Bagger 258 are an Augsburg-based German EBM duo formed by Nico von der Eisenmühle and Tim “Hacke” Schmelzer. Their debut album “Aufwärts gehts bergab” was released in February 2026 and includes remixes by Nachtmahr, NordarR and Menticide; Side-Line covered the album in a March 2024 interview with the duo. Cygnosic is the Athens-based dark-electro project of Georgios Psaroudakis. “Demystify” appeared in 2023 as the project’s seventh full-length album, while 2025’s “Theorem” revisited Cygnosic compositions through metal arrangements without abandoning the project’s electronic core. Side-Line first covered the Nachtmahr connection in 2019, when Cygnosic toured with Nachtmahr and labelmates C-lekktor behind the “Epiphany” LP. Nachtmahr, founded by Austrian musician Thomas Rainer in 2007, has developed a distinctive language around hard electronic rhythm, theatrical authority, confrontation, discipline and increasingly broad stylistic freedom. IMPERIVM is the latest stage of that development, while the current tour is the largest and longest undertaken under the Nachtmahr name. The Wrocław opening showed how carefully the three-band construction worked: Bagger 258 established the body, Cygnosic changed the way it moved, and Nachtmahr took control of what had already been set in motion. By the end, the contradiction Thomas Rainer and I had discussed before the tour, extreme control on one side of the stage and deliberate surrender on the other, no longer needed explaining. It was visible everywhere in the room.

items.body: Winter Sect have discovered one of goth’s better-kept secrets: graveyards can be funny places. Not funny in the sitcom sense, unless your sitcom happens to involve velvet sleeves, low fog, marble angels, and a bass player turning cemetery dirt into a dance floor, but funny in the grand old rock-and-roll sense that the concept of memento mori has always looked a little less terrifying once somebody places a wreath of backbeat on the coffin. Made up of Sister Ex alumna Claudia Neuman on bass and vocals, guitarist Anthony Piazza, keyboardist and vocalist Heather Wayward, and drummer Darryl J. Dardenne, the DC/Baltimore group have previously favored the colder end of Gothic psychedelia and glam rock. Graveyard Girl, however, loosens the corset. Funk, garage rock, indie pop and even bossa nova slip into the bloodstream, bringing a loose, easy groove beneath the song’s ’60s pop whimsy while the band keeps one boot planted firmly in post-punk soil. Neuman’s bass is responsible for the initial crime, strutting around with the casual confidence of someone who has found the liquor cabinet during a wake. Wayward’s keyboards add splashes of color around Piazza’s guitar, while Dardenne keeps the song moving with a lightness that gives its cemetery imagery room to grin. The melody has the cheeky charm of a vintage pop single, its tuneful bounce making the invitation to wander among the graves sound suspiciously like a proposition for a Sunday afternoon date. Siouxsie and the Banshees, March Violets, Strange Boutique and more hover somewhere in the family tree, although Winter Sect sound especially amused by the possibilities of their own material here. According to Wayward, that playful turn happened almost accidentally during rehearsal: “The song pretty much started with Claudia grooving out on a bass line,” she says. “It was catchy and I thought let’s do something completely different and not so serious and macabre. First the hook was discovered and we built from there. So with that funk of a groove my mind started walking. Where? Through the graveyard of course. It came together in a cool way and a little twist at the end just makes it fun.” That sense of fun carries into the video, which sends the band wandering through the necropolis in slow motion among candles, veils and fog. Somebody communes with the departed, everybody looks appropriately dressed for the occasion, and the solemn machinery of Gothic imagery gains a sly little wink. You half expect one of the headstones to start keeping time. Watch the video for Graveyard Girl below: Winter Sect began in late 2023 when California native Neuman and Piazza formed the project around feedback-heavy goth, New Wave, industrial and psychedelic influences. Mystic Twin and Haunted House followed in 2024, with Say Goodbye appearing in 2026. Graveyard Girl, taken from the forthcoming EP Offering, suggests Winter Sect have figured out that darkness becomes far more interesting when somebody remembers to leave room for mischief and a tune you can hum on the way home. Dardenne 则以轻盈的节奏为墓地意象留出呼吸空间。旋律具有六十年代流行的俏皮魅力，使游荡于墓地的邀约听起来像周末午后的约会。乐队此前的风格偏冷峻的哥特迷幻与华丽摇滚，而这张作品明显松开了束缚，在保持后朋克骨架的同时引入了更多元的律动与幽默感。MV 以慢动作呈现乐队在蜡烛、面纱与薄雾中的游走，让哥特意象多了一丝狡黠的眨眼。这支来自 DC/Baltimore 地区的四人组成立于 2023 年末，融合了反馈厚重的哥特、新浪潮、工业与迷幻影响，《Graveyard Girl》展现了他们在不牺牲黑暗气质的前提下拥抱更多可能性的方向。

items.body: Lift the veil, see what I’ve become An exoskeletal pantheon Born again from bone and breath To spread the living gospel of death On Tears for the Dying‘s blistering new gothic track Devour Me, Adria Stembridge drags the band back toward its earlier roots with a slower, heavier gait, then breaks that crawl apart with abrupt tempo changes that make the song feel unstable beneath your feet. Stembridge handles drum machine, guitar, bass, and vocals, building the track from dark guitar figures, blunt low-end pressure, and drums that move with the patience of something following you home. Her vocals hang above it all in a cold echo, less concerned with theatrical grandstanding than with letting the words rot in the air for a second before the next image lands. You can hear Bauhaus in the skeletal guitar work, Alien Sex Fiend in the queasy theatricality, and PiL and Fields of the Nephilim in the sense that somebody has wandered far enough from civilization to start inventing a religion. That religious impulse becomes central once the lyrics start opening the trapdoor. Stembridge draws from cosmic horror, but the terror here feels brutally physical. A solitary figure encounters an impossible swarm, loses control of the body piece by piece, and becomes host to something that treats flesh as raw material. Bones break. Insects burrow. The victim survives only in the technical sense, gradually becoming an alien deity whose transformation has erased whatever person existed before. The nastiest idea arrives afterward: worship. What begins as predation becomes conversion, and the ruined body becomes scripture. Consumption, reproduction, faith, and extermination collapse together until divinity itself starts looking like another parasitic infection. There is something wonderfully foul about that conception of godhood, especially coming from a band whose Southern gothic deathrock has long carried radical queer politics alongside its horror imagery. Authority here comes crawling out of meat. The slower passages give those images room to breathe before the faster sections shove everything toward panic. That contrast is crucial. Speed alone would turn the song into pursuit; the deliberate sections make you wait for whatever is chewing through the floorboards. By the final transformation, cosmic horror has lost every trace of abstraction. Infinity sprouts mandibles, theology breeds larvae, and salvation becomes a forced rebirth inside a body that has been converted into temple, nursery, and weapon. items.body: The screams of children, far away Echo in this perfect day A perfect society becomes considerably harder to admire once somebody explains who has been paying for it. In Ursula K. Le Guin’s The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas, an entire city’s happiness depends upon the suffering of a single child, an arrangement its citizens learn to accept as the price of their good fortune. There is plenty of room for horror in that cheerful consensus, especially once the people benefiting from it begin explaining why things simply have to be this way. Bologna’s La Mano Sinistra, whose name means “the left hand” in Italian, take up that ugly bargain on their debut single, Unnecessary Perfection. The track introduces Omelas, a seven-track concept album due November 6, 2026, through Bat-Cave Productions, translating Le Guin’s ethical dilemma into gothic rock with enough melodic momentum to carry its uncomfortable questions straight onto the dancefloor. A heartbeat rhythm opens the track, its alternating accents pressing against sustained, cold synthesizer tones before a thick, low-slung bassline sends everything forward. Guitar and electronics give the melody a generous sweep while Davide Sacco sings with the decadent authority of a frontman who can make a warning sound almost inviting. The combination brings to mind The Danse Society around their Heaven Is Waiting era, with something of Children on Stun and Brotherhood of Pagans in the vocal delivery and the way the instruments lock together. The guitar break ascends and descends through the melody, supplying an exhilarating lift while sustaining the chill of the surrounding synths. When Sacco’s voice returns alongside it, a more romantic quality enters his timbre, adding a strange tenderness to the accusation. This is the kind of gothic rock that makes getting dressed to go out feel like the opening scene of an evening full of possibilities. For a song about the moral cost of everybody having a good time, it has a wicked talent for getting the evening started. The lyrics initially survey a population blessed with sharp minds, untouched lives, and the promise of a cure for all, while concealed currents move beneath that reassuring surface. Sacco’s recurring question, “What’s necessary, what is not,” unsettles the supposed inevitability of the arrangement. By the closing lines, children’s screams carry across the distance into the perfect day itself. Read alongside Le Guin’s story, that distance becomes part of the accusation: comfort depends upon keeping suffering far enough away to be tolerated, even when its beneficiaries know exactly what sustains their happiness. The band describe the single this way: “The paradox of perfection. A fast-paced, impactful track reflecting the fictitious tranquility of a society built upon the distant screams of the weakest.” The accompanying video gives that selective vision an effective visual counterpart. High-contrast black-and-white performance footage is crossed by horizontal bands that repeatedly interrupt faces, instruments, and the lyrics appearing on screen. Close-ups of hands working the strings alternate with Sacco at the microphone, while the bars make even the plainest words momentarily difficult to see. The treatment suggests an uncomfortable connection between an obstructed image and a society accustomed to accepting a partial view. Watch the video for Unnecessary Perfection below: La Mano Sinistra brings together Sacco on vocals and lyrics, Gianluca Lo Presti of Nevica on bass and electronics, and Giuseppe Lo Bue of Caron Dimonio on guitar and electronics. Sacco is also a co-founder of the contemporary theatre company ErosAntEros and artistic director of POLIS Teatro Festival, a background that gives the project’s theatrical character a clear foundation. Omelas grew out of Sacco’s stage production of The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas, performed by actress Eva Robin’s. Recorded at Loto Studio in Ravenna during the summer of 2025, the album develops its source material across seven chapters, addressing indifference, collective guilt, and the decision to abandon a prosperity built upon injustice for an uncertain life beyond it. Unnecessary Perfection is available on digital platforms. Omelas follows on November 6, 2026, via Bat-Cave Productions. items._cn_summary: 意大利波伦亚三人组合以乌苏拉·勒古恩的短篇小说《奥美拉斯》为概念核心，将道德困境转化为哥特摇滚的肢体律动。开场以心跳般的节奏与冷调合成器铺垫，低沉贝斯线驱动整首歌曲前行，旋律在电子与人声之间获得宽阔的呼吸空间。主唱萨科的声线带有颓废的权威感，使警告听起来近乎诱惑；间奏吉他段在旋律中攀升与回落，既维持了合成器的寒意又带来振奋的飞跃。歌词审视一个拥有清醒心智、未被触及的生命与万灵药承诺的完美社会，反复追问何为必要、何为多余，结尾时孩童的尖叫穿越距离渗入完美的白昼。视觉方面采用高对比度黑白现场影像，与歌曲所揭示的选择性视野形成对应。整体呈现出将文学伦理议题与舞池可听性结合的独特处理方式。

items.excerpt: 『ピアノ・ホライズン』に80年代の日本の音楽シーンを垣間見る。ローズからモールス信号のような単音の連打が聴こえ、クラヴィのクラスターが連打を断ち切る。ファンキーな音色にマイルス・デイヴィスの音楽のようだと感じるが、リズムにグルーヴが感じられるわけではない。松平頼暁がこのアルバムを企画したピアニスト里見暁美に書き下ろした“エリクサトーン”だ。しばらくしてピアノが緩やかに辿る下降音形が聴こえ、そこに時折りピアノからの異音が混じり、雨後のアスファルトから昇る蒸気のような音場が立ち上がる。藤枝守の“フォーリング・スケール第6番”だ。この二人の作品は〈表現内容よりも構造が強調〉されていると近藤譲はノートに記す。

items._genre: contemporary classical / experimental piano / avant-garde composition
items._cn_summary: 这张1981年的专辑聚焦日本现代钢琴作品，通过松平頼暁的《エリクサトーン》和藤枝守的《フォーリング・スケール第6番》展示80年代日本音乐场景中实验性的一面。前者以玫瑰般的单音连打开场，仿若密码电报与鼓点节奏的交织，音色透出爵士质感却刻意削弱了传统律动感；后者以钢琴的缓降音形铺展底色，不协和异音渗入其中，营造出雨后路面蒸腾般的氛围。两位作曲家被近藤譲评价为'结构优先于表现内容'，意味着音乐更关注材料组织与声响关系本身。该专辑适合对当代古典与实验音乐交汇领域感兴趣的听众，为理解日本战后现代音乐脉络提供了一个具体切片。

items.body: Wardruna’s wonderful performance at London’s Union Chapel was a heavy vision of their might and majesty. One unstoppable note became a potent portal, leading to other, northern realms brimming with the threat of fire and the glimmer of ice. Their performance was an almost transcendent experience rooted in Norse spiritualism and the elements of fire, water and earth. This wasn’t Norway (they played two nights here as part of their European tour), but it could’ve been. The music was somehow both ancient and contemporary, sculpted by sharp blades and fearsome weaponry. It was also equally founded in love: for music, for tradition, for culture, for people. It fed on its own history and drank from the cup of the present, standing partly in lost centuries and partly in new, fertile ground, and that came across with every ground-pounding thump of a deer-hide drum. At first, a pair of gigantic horns flanked the stage, looking like great monuments that should be worshipped and respected, each one presenting a gate to be entered. One note can open everything, and the vocals soon lit up the space like a set of stark torches; together they carried a flame that burnt brightly. Harmonies came into being, with both Einar Selvik’s and Lindy Fay Hella’s all-encompassing vocals soaring to stratospheric levels and then diving deep into the earth. Materialising out of the earth was a dark kind of Nordic folk, but enriched with elements that were beyond classification. The music was full of power and passion, somehow older than everything else and yet incredibly fresh. At one point, faces were lit in the crimson of blood, like the prom scene from Carrie. The stringed instruments plucked out melodies composed of the lightest air, while other melodies flicked tongues of fire that tasted like copper and spewed out jets of molten flame. The lyrics glowed like warm flares against the Nordic night. The heavy, marching drums were like the racing hooves of ten thousand horses, all honing in on a certain, key point. It was the sound of war, the sound of battle, with music being the weapon. The chilly and piercing sound of a goat horn punctured the air, and the red-blooded, thunderous drums wound themselves up again, ready to pump more energy into the steady pounding of a restless heart. Other genres use these rhythms a lot, too – rhythm is just as crucial in today’s modern-era of house and electronic music as it was a thousand years ago and even earlier – but sometimes other, additional rhythms were woven in, making them ornate, complex and deep. Rain and thunder became an ominous premonition in the sound, the horn slowly drowning under the weight of a rain-drenched harmony that was as black as the night. The lyrics were conductors of heat and protectors against the cold air. Robed shadows lit up the walls, and like a procession of spirits from the past they marched in place, absorbing into the swelling harmonies, the stark intervals and the intensely delivered lyrics. Nothing was held back, because music such as this can never be tamed. The only way to truly experience it is to fully unleash it, to have the hood that covers its skull pulled back, revealing its face. The music reached an unstoppable, mighty crescendo before a scream that could tear flesh from bone shattered the air, but even among the more intense segments there were always moments of contemplation and relative peace – a period of change and calm – brought forth by a slower tempo or more of a sobering atmosphere. Something was always brewing, though. Strobing lights dazzled the audience and circular orbs of a softer light stretched their arms up to the heavens. Smoky, shrill horns and a steady, slow drum helped to shape a dense and ever-shifting atmosphere. This was the ultimate offering and another testimony to the power of music – songs of life and songs of death, songs of every experience, uniting everyone with their potency. It was an emotional performance that at times bordered on the euphoric. The final song was one about death, but it was also about our place in this life. It wasn’t a solemn ending but a triumphant one, a reassurance that the spirit of the music will always live on and embrace come what may, even after the soul has departed. Wardruna have a warm love for London and the city responded in kind with a lengthy standing ovation which the music and the performing artistry fully deserved. Photos: Nick Sayers www.wardruna.com www.unionchapel.org.uk
items._genre: Nordic folk / ritual music / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了Wardruna在伦敦Union Chapel的现场演出，以北欧异教精神为核心，将火、水、土等自然元素融入音乐。表演融合了古老传统与当代审美，鹿皮鼓、羊角号、弦乐器与人声交织，构建出既古老又崭新的听觉图景。Einar Selvik与Lindy Fay Hella的人声从高耸的和声层直入地底深处，弦乐轻拨出如空气般的旋律，鼓声如万马奔腾般沉重行进。歌词如北欧黑夜中的温暖火焰，抵御寒意。整体演出超越了传统民谣范畴，融合了无法归类的元素，节奏复杂而精雕细琢，雨水与雷声成为不祥预兆，和声在夜色中沉沉铺展。这是一场扎根于文化与传统的沉浸式仪式演出。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 专辑《Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea》以十九世纪加州墨西哥牛仔远赴夏威夷放牧的历史为线索，将墨西哥与夏威夷两地音乐传统并置。16首曲目涵盖西班牙语、夏威夷语和英语演唱，包含老夏威夷歌曲配西班牙语新词、老墨西哥歌曲配夏威夷语新词、新创作以及传统美式民谣。核心乐器为尤克里里、吉他、墨西哥竖琴和手风琴，密集编排形成统一声响。Taj Mahal与David Hidalgo作为核心人物参与选曲、编排和多乐器演奏，并与夏威夷本地歌手及乐手合作。录音在加州圣巴勃罗的总部以同期方式完成，仅用五天，大量学生参与录制，营造出即兴化的现场感与自发氛围。整体强调语言、文化、年龄和性别的多元协作，呈现墨西哥与夏威夷丰富且被固有印象化的音乐文化。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦圣多美和普林西比这两个大西洋小岛在1970至80年代录制的Puxa音乐。该风格融合了多个前葡萄牙语非洲殖民地的音乐元素，并吸收了merengue、苏库斯、班加等加勒比与非洲节奏，被认为具有召灵驱邪的仪式功能。葡萄牙殖民者百年前曾禁止Puxa舞蹈，但显然未能奏效。专辑收录15首作品，呈现多把吉他交织缠绕、人声与旋律框架相互呼应的特点，贝斯与键盘退场时鼓与吉他仍能驱动舞池。Pedro Lima领衔的乐队以压缩吉他和鼓组展开激烈对话，Sangazuza则展示了纯节奏驱动下的狂热律动。作为Volume 1的延续，这套编录将小岛有限录音条件下的音乐成果集中呈现，为世界音乐听众提供了稀有的非洲边缘岛屿之声。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑融合了民谣、前卫音乐与中世纪圣咏的质感，Alison Cotton 以中提琴、簧风琴、击弦古钢琴与钢琴为核心乐器，加入鼓、贝斯与合成器扩展音色边界。多数作品为一次性即兴录制，保留了某种神秘而低语的氛围感。John Clare 的诗作被谱入旋律，在持续低音之上展开超脱的声线；《Sprigs of Heather》以中世纪宗教音乐式的开场引入钢琴主导的缓慢级进旋律，结构凝练。专辑同时也是对其2024年末去世父亲的悼念之作，《The Final Harvest》以庄严笔触描绘父亲最后一次前往他所热爱的菜地，情感充盈而克制。光与暗在不同曲目间交替渗透，音乐拒绝被归类，在多种风格暗示之间保持自身的辨识度，呈现为一种跨时空的聆听体验。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这是挪威Camilla Hole Trio的第二张专辑，相比前作与科幻合成器的大胆结合，此作回归更为朴素的民间音乐根基。主奏乐器高音萨克斯将爵士语汇注入挪威西部传统春季舞曲「Springleik」，贝斯手Egil Kalman与鼓手Knut Kvifte Nesheim以模块合成器和颤音琴叠加音色层次。三人角色不断流动互换——Kalman接替主奏旋律与Hole齐奏，Nesheim则拓展节奏空间——使整首作品走向即兴化展开。专辑延续了超越本土民乐框架的探索，将传统旋律素材置于自由即兴的语境中重新结构，模块合成器作为色彩层渗透于原声乐器之间，形成有机而不拘一格的声响质感。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由瑞典小提琴手、挪威竖笛/萨克斯演奏家及鼓手组成的北欧跨界三重奏专辑，以非常规方式重新演绎斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲。乐评将作品比作室内乐——三位乐手沉浸在亲密的音乐对话中，而非用于伴舞的演奏。编曲在保留舞曲旋律骨架的同时，通过即兴化的和声层叠、纹理化伴奏和碎片化结构揭示音乐暗藏的深层意涵。选曲上以挪威塞特斯达尔小提琴曲《Fossgrimen》开场，暗喻传统背后的黑暗面。短曲中旋律与伴奏在推进过程中逐渐瓦解，呈现出解构与重构并存的实验质感。挪威独立小厂牌发行，整体融合世界音乐底色与前卫即兴手法。

items._cn_summary: 本篇为The Squid's Ear近期评论合集，涵盖自由即兴、当代作曲与实验爵士三大领域。其中Ivo Perelman与Matthew Shipp的《Duologues 7: Distillation》作为两人长期合作项目的最新篇章，评论者Marc Medwin着重分析了二人三十年来逐渐形成的亲密即兴语言，以及在调性蓝调结构与完全自由发明之间的持续流动。该专辑延续了二人一贯的二元对话形式，萨克斯与钢琴在限定框架内展开即兴博弈，文本本身偏短，仅能窥见该系列创作脉络的一角。整体而言，这是一组面向小众听众的高度专业化即兴与当代音乐评论汇编，聚焦于声音探索与即兴美学，适合对实验即兴音乐有持续关注的听众参考。

items.excerpt: Is Woven Ground an EP with an accompanying film, or a film with an accompanying EP? We’ll leave it to the project’s viewers and listeners and to decide. items.body: Is Woven Ground an EP with an accompanying film, or a film with an accompanying EP? We’ll leave it to the project’s viewers and listeners and to decide. Either way, Blair Coron‘s multi-media release is a treat for the eyes and ears, a celebration of Scottish forests, islands and glens, filled with lush instrumentation, poetry and harmony, coupled with sumptuous landscapes and insightful interviews. As Coron explains, “I could never say, ‘This song is the river’ or ‘these words are the forest’ … so I took my instruments and recording equipment and friends to the places I was writing about.” The landscapes are first seen from a moving car, then the disembarking, revealing the sounds of the village and the port. In the early minutes, Coron celebrates the gift of the Isle of Canna, a sacred trust and sanctuary. The cows seem as relaxed as the strings and historical piano, or the other way around. The views are bucolic, the pace of life unhurried, the area seemingly free from pollution, time in suspension. The natural soundscape is allowed to take center stage (more detectable in the film than the EP). In the first interview, one learns of apple trees fertilized by the bodies of seals. Farmland equipment lies abandoned; an ancient church stands witness. Local residents express pride in their location and history. Shoes off, windows open, Coron engages with the piano; “Isle of Canna, Midsummer, 5:54am, 2026” arrives a third of the way into the film, but is the EP’s opening piece, a love letter to the location. The next piece takes a little more work; a harmonium is not an easy instrument to move, especially across uneven terrain. The sprightly “Sgùrr A’ Mhaoraich” is performed by a babbling brook, with Charlie Stewart on the much more portable fiddle. The piece is an ode to the countryside and the flowing water, whose music never ends. As the camera zooms in to the reel-to-reel, the recording device begins to look like a stream. Coron sits outdoors at a table, reciting “Beneath Six Black Poplar Trees,” a poem that looks back to the dawn of creation, with creation itself the accompaniment. His voice is comforting, with gentle inflection that matches the spider webs undulating in the wind. The strings return, setting up the gorgeous closer, which includes Miwa Nagato-Apthorp and Zoe Bestel on layered vocals. “Hymn,” while not on the EP, is one of the highlights of the film (35:12-38:06, a music video on its own). An adjacent version was released on the Two Old Songs EP in April, the original on On the Nature of Things, but we like this choral version the best. For “Moon Lament,” the quartet sits in the woods, captivated and captivating, having become part of the visual and sonic scenery, melting into the forest like the voices of the water and the wind. This ebullient song is chased by warm laughter and the twittering of birds; the camera draws back, revealing canopies of green. Woven Ground the EP becomes a souvenir of Woven Ground the film. The images resurface when playing the music, stored in the memory as the seeds are stored in the earth. (Richard Allen)
items._genre: folk / field recording / contemporary classical / ambient
items._cn_summary: Blair Coron的《Woven Ground》是一部结合音乐与影像的多媒体作品，以苏格兰森林、岛屿与峡谷为背景。创作者将乐器与录音设备带入实地，在自然声场中完成演奏与录制：钢琴、手风琴、小提琴与诗歌朗诵与溪流、鸟鸣、海岸风声交织。影像部分记录了坎纳岛的风土与居民访谈，呈现苹果树、海豹遗骸、古老教堂等地方记忆。部分作品有合唱层叠的版本，在林中演绎时人与乐器仿佛融入环境。整体介于民谣采风与现代作曲之间，强调场域特殊性而非纯粹音乐实验，影像叙事为作品增加了感官维度。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Shifting from the brutal to the delicate within a single song - one of the hallmarks that Opeth handled with ease - reached a turning point with the groundbreaking "Damnation" (2003), an album that almost entirely dispenses with the hostile sounds of extreme metal to embrace the most melodic aspects of '70s progressive rock. A risky decision that, despite initial concerns, demonstrated the band's versatility in moving confidently between different musical styles, while leaving fans and critics alike wondering about the direction the band would take in the future.With "Ghost Reveries" (2005), their eighth album, the Swedes once again use death metal as one of the fundamental elements of their sound, integrated with progressive components that are far more developed than in their previous works. Mikael �kerfeldt's demonic growls, the monolithic and dense guitar riffs of Peter Lindgren and �kerfeldt - which evoke extreme bands like Morbid Angel, the more experimental Tool, or the classic Black Sabbath, among others - and a powerful instrumental foundation alternate and blend with deep, clean vocals, crystalline acoustic elements, and Per Wiberg's hypnotic and cosmic keyboards, to construct a sonic tapestry of contrasts and shifts in intensity that moves naturally between ferocity and a hypnotic, enveloping melancholy."Ghost of Perdition", "The Baying of the Hounds" - featuring evocative Jon Lord-style organ - and the oriental-inspired "Beneath the Mire" unfold across expansive instrumental valleys and peaks that showcase the band's maturity, and find their full expression in "Reverie / Harlequin Forest" - featuring superb clean and harmonic phrasing by �kerfeldt - and, above all, in the ritualistic and intriguing "The Grand Conjuration" - reminiscent at times of Pink Floyd's "Echoes" - the album's finest moments.And the influence of "Damnation" is also present and can be felt in the tremulous "Atonement" and "Hours of Wealth," with their keyboards and a certain jazzy flair, and in the closing "Isolation Years," with its acoustic and dreamlike character, featuring �kerfeldt's whispering vocals and Lindgren's arpeggios, ultimately shaping the excellent "Ghost Reveries", one of Opeth's finest albums and standing alongside the iconic "Still Life" and "Blackwater Park".4/4.5 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / death metal / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: Opeth第八张录音室专辑在极端金属与七十年代前卫摇滚之间游走，以猛烈死亡金属咆哮与清澈人声、键盘、原声段落形成强烈对比。乐评聚焦于乐队如何在前作纯旋律化探索之后重新引入金属元素，吉他厚重层叠受Morbid Angel与Black Sabbath影响，键盘营造出宇宙感氛围，歌曲如《The Grand Conjuration》被类比为Pink Floyd式回响。专辑将《Damnation》中的柔美与早期作品残暴融合为一，既有冲击性的极端段落也有爵士色彩键盘小品与梦幻原声尾曲。乐评将其定位为乐队最佳之一，评论质量详实，对器乐编排与情感张力的交替有清晰分析。作为跨界融合的前卫金属，接近实验/前卫口味但偏向金属根脉，有一定跨类型探索但非深度的实验性创新。

items.excerpt: エミル・パリジャン、タブラと交わる新作『Floating』 ヨーロッパジャズのソプラノサックス奏者として25年のキャリアを築いてきたエミル・パリジャンが、ACTレーベルから新作『Floating』をリリースした。ピアノのヤロン・ハーマン、ベースのリンダ・メイ・ハン・オー、そしてタブラ奏者プラブ・エドゥアールとの共演による本作は、古典音楽から世界音楽まで幅広い影響を吸収してきたパリジャンの語法が、非西洋の打楽器といかに対話するかを示す一枚だ。 France Musiqueのポッドキャストで語られた制作の背景によれば、この邂逅は偶発的なコラボレーションというより、長年培われてきた音楽的語彙の延長線上にあるという。ジャズがヨーロッパの文脈でどう自己更新を続けてきたか、その現在地を示す作品とも言えるだろう。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/emile-parisien-6403447 コルトレーン生誕100年に、マルサリスとリーヴスが応えた新作 ジョン・コルトレーン生誕100周年を記念し
items.body: エミル・パリジャン、タブラと交わる新作『Floating』 ヨーロッパジャズのソプラノサックス奏者として25年のキャリアを築いてきたエミル・パリジャンが、ACTレーベルから新作『Floating』をリリースした。ピアノのヤロン・ハーマン、ベースのリンダ・メイ・ハン・オー、そしてタブラ奏者プラブ・エドゥアールとの共演による本作は、古典音楽から世界音楽まで幅広い影響を吸収してきたパリジャンの語法が、非西洋の打楽器といかに対話するかを示す一枚だ。 France Musiqueのポッドキャストで語られた制作の背景によれば、この邂逅は偶発的なコラボレーションというより、長年培われてきた音楽的語彙の延長線上にあるという。ジャズがヨーロッパの文脈でどう自己更新を続けてきたか、その現在地を示す作品とも言えるだろう。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/emile-parisien-6403447 コルトレーン生誕100年に、マルサリスとリーヴスが応えた新作 ジョン・コルトレーン生誕100周年を記念し、ブランフォード・マルサリス四重奏団とヴォーカリストのディアンヌ・リーヴスが、Blue Noteから新作『Dedicated To You』をリリースした。企画の出発点にあるのは、1963年の名盤『John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman』——テナーサックスとバラード・ヴォーカルという編成そのものを引き継ぎながら、長年の相棒であるピアニスト、ジョーイ・カルデラッツォらとの即興的なアレンジ作業を通じて、バラード解釈を更新したという。 生誕100年という節目に、過去の名盤をなぞるのではなく、その成り立ちに立ち返って新たな即興性を持ち込んだ点に、今回の企画の芯があるとも言える。既存の敬意の示し方とは異なる道を選んだ一枚として、聴き比べる価値がありそうだ。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/branford-marsalis-quartet-dianne-reeves-eternellement-coltrane-8964069 ビートメイカー、キーファーがBlue Noteからデビュー ロサンゼルスのビート・カルチャーと結びつきの深いビートメイカー、キーファーが、名門Blue Noteから『Memory Bomb』と題したデビューアルバムをリリースした。ジャズとヒップホップ、ロサンゼルスのビート・カルチャーを融合させた作品で、ジャジーヒップホップの現在地を示す一枚として評されている。Blue Noteという老舗レーベルがビートメイカーの作品を迎え入れた背景について、今後の展開にも注視したい一作だ。 出典：https://glidemagazine.com/330465/kiefer-turns-jazz-hip-hop-and-l-a-beat-culture-into-blue-note-debut-titled-memory-bomb-album-review ニューオーリンズ、音と食が共存する理由 米国ニューオーリンズで、音楽と料理に関わる2人の共著による新刊『Rhythm & Roux』が出版された。著者のブライアン・ランドリーとピーター・ハリスは、著名なシェフと卓越した音楽家のコンビだ。 ニューオーリンズでは、音楽と食が別々の娯楽としてではなく、同じ場所・同じ共同体の記憶として息づいてきた。本書はその結びつきを、単なる郷土料理本としてではなく、ニューオーリンズの食と音楽がどのように共に進化してきたのかを描き出す。 出典：https://www.npr.org/2026/09/20/nx-s1-5940782/cookbook-rhythm-and-roux-brian-landry-peter-harris スティーヴィー・ワンダー『Songs in the Key of Life』の未発表曲を公開 スティーヴィー・ワンダーがアルバム『Songs in the Key of Life』の50周年を記念し、同アルバムの膨大なセッションから未発表曲を収録したEPをリリースした。 1976年にリリースされた『Songs in the Key of Life』は、スティーヴン・ワンダーに3度目のグラミー賞最優秀アルバム賞をもたらし、「I Wish」「Isn’t She Lovely」「As」「Sir Duke」といった現代のスタンダードナンバーを収録。ハービー・ハンコック、ジョージ・ベンソン、ミニー・リパートンなど多くのアーティストが参加している。 出典：https://pitchfork.com/story/stevie-wonder-unvaults-four-songs-in-the-key-of-life-tracks 今週すでにお伝えしたニュース 海野雅威がオスカー・ピーターソンの名盤『We Get Requests』に捧げるトリビュート公演を開催 【ジャズフェスカレンダー2026】10月／11月／12月開催のジャズフェスティバル＆イベント ロンドン発のアンチアルゴリズム音楽プラットフォーム「ROVR」─日本初のフェス&レコードフェアを新木場で開催 【石川紅奈｜インタビュー】“心の中の庭” で芽吹いた大切なものをあつめて─新アルバム『Garden』発表 投稿 【ARBAN WEEKLY｜今週の話題まとめ】キーファーがBlue Noteからデビュー／パリジャンとタブラの対話／スティービー・ワンダー名盤の未発表曲／ほか は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items._cn_summary: 本篇为多则音乐新闻的合集，涵盖五项内容：法国爵士萨克斯演奏家埃米尔·巴黎疆与塔布拉鼓手合作的新专辑《Floating》，探索欧洲爵士语汇与非西方打击乐的对话；布兰福德·马萨利斯四重奏与歌手戴安·里夫斯为纪念约翰·科尔特兰诞辰百年发行新作《Dedicated To You》，延续经典编制并融入即兴编排；洛杉矶制作人Kiefer以《Memory Bomb》在Blue Note首张专辑，融合爵士与嘻-hop及城市节拍文化；新奥尔良音乐与饮食文化交融的新书《Rhythm & Roux》；以及史提夫·汪达《Songs in the Key of Life》五十周年纪念EP，公开未发行录音。整体以新闻汇编形式呈现，涉及欧洲爵士即兴、世界音乐融合及主流厂牌项目。

items.body: Tangent Strategy announces “Tristesse”, the project’s first new full-length album in five years. The album is inspired by the music of John Foxx and Die Form. “Tristesse” explores the fragile human psyche, where anger and melancholy sit next to each other. It looks at the defiance inside relationships, healthy and unhealthy alike, and the marks they leave on the people in them. Production-wise, the album takes a simpler approach than before, keeping the songs raw with deep bass, stark arrangements and noise running through the mix. “In an age of detachment, Tristesse is a reminder that attachment is no certain comfort either,” the project states. Tristesse by Tangent Strategy About Tangent Strategy Tangent Strategy was formed in 1996 by chd.y as an outlet for a musical outlook that grew more and more drawn to industrial music over the years. The project’s first full-length, “Revenant”, came out in November 2021 via EK Product. Since then, chd.y has released several EPs under the name and performed live in Tokyo. “Tristesse”, announced in 2026, is Tangent Strategy’s second full-length album.

items.body: Belgian electronic artist Franky Deblomme releases a new EP as Cubic, “Elements,” on October 2, 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The five-track digital release moves the project’s minimal electro sound into more dynamic techno territory. Elements EP by CUBIC ‘Elements’ draws on 80s electro, 90s techno and dub techno “Elements” draws on 1980s electro, 1990s techno in the style of R&S Records, and acid and dub techno, the reference points that have run through Cubic’s sound over the years, with Alfa Matrix noting a nod toward contemporary acts such as Bicep and Modeselektor. Opening track “Future Past” and the two versions of “BangBang,” a Detroit edit and a Chicago edit, push the EP toward a more dancefloor-oriented, energetic direction. “A Fish” and “Chord Memory” keep the minimal sequences, vintage electronics and repeating patterns that recur through Cubic’s releases. ‘Elements’ EP tracklist “Future Past” (4:31) “BangBang” (Detroit edit) (4:26) “A Fish” (4:35) “Chord Memory” (4:55) “BangBang” (Chicago edit) (4:10) The EP is a digital release, available as a download via the Alfa Matrix Bandcamp page, with streaming included, at up to 24-bit/44.1kHz. About Cubic Cubic is the electronic project of Belgian artist Franky Deblomme, also known for his earlier work as 808 Dot Pop. Deblomme signed Cubic to Alfa Matrix and released the project’s label debut EP, “Alphabet Hymn,” on March 9, 2021. The five-track EP combined vintage Dusseldorf synth influences, Berlin techno, 1990s Manchester rave and EBM, built entirely on hardware synthesizers and effects at Deblomme’s Bong 13 studio, and included a remix by label mates 808 Dot Pop. Later that month, Cubic reworked an earlier 808 Dot Pop album into “The Cubic Temperature,” released March 26, 2021 with an exclusive Bandcamp megamix bonus track. Cubic’s debut album, “The Cubic Alphabet,” arrived on June 18, 2021. The project continued with the EP “Phonic Lessons Part 3” on December 7, 2021, then the singles “Exit – Frankfurt” on April 7, 2022 and the four-track “Exit – Ghent” on June 29, 2022, each tied to a specific city’s electronic scene. The EPs “c64” (September 18, 2023) and “c128” (December 6, 2023), both referencing Commodore home computers, preceded the album “Back To Basic,” released on Alfa Matrix on June 4, 2024 with a Kraftwerk-indebted sound made using the first Belgian-made drum computer (Modor DR2) and synthesizer (Modor NF1). Cubic released the vinyl EP “EFM01 (Black)” in an ultra-limited run in June 2025, then the digital EP “EFM02” in October 2025 and the rework album “Back To 808” in December 2025. The twin EPs “CB-708” and “CB-128,” revisiting “Back To 808,” came out in February 2026. “Elements,” out October 2, 2026, is Cubic’s newest EP on Alfa Matrix. items.body: Belgian EBM act Implant releases the EP “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” on October 2, 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The eight-track release previews the band’s fifteenth studio album, “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” due October 30 on the same label. I’m Only Happy When You Bleed EP by IMPLANT ‘I’m Only Happy When You Bleed’ is the second single from ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ The title track is the second song revealed from “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” after lead single “Underneath The Neon Lights.” Built on a 3/4 rhythm, it pairs evolving electronic layers and a shifting pulse with lyrics centered on control, cruelty and forced submission. The EP extends the single into an eight-track release. “Information Systems” opens the record with a long-form soundscape built entirely from spoken samples about the mythology of computing. “The Insider” addresses privileged knowledge and how much of what people take as fact is actually interpretation or assumption. “Pills (in f sharp)” reworks the album track “Pills” into a different key, turning its “I want more pills” refrain into both a chant and a comment on the pursuit of quick fixes. “Underneath The Neon Lights” also appears on the EP. Three remixes of the title track close the release. New York act Crash Course In Science turns the song into a club-oriented dance track. People Theatre take it in a more melodic direction before a detuned lead takes over. Belgian label mate Aiboforcen contributes a version Alfa Matrix describes as distinctly Aiboforcen’s own while staying rooted in Implant’s sound. ‘I’m Only Happy When You Bleed’ EP tracklist “Information Systems” (3:16) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (4:00) “Underneath The Neon Lights” (4:55) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (Crash Course In Science remix) (4:39) “Pills (in f sharp)” (4:00) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (People Theatre vein remix) (5:32) “The Insider” (4:33) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (Aiboforcen remix) (4:12) The EP is a digital release, available as a download in MP3 and FLAC via the Alfa Matrix Bandcamp page, with streaming included, at up to 16-bit/44.1kHz. ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ follows on October 30 Side-Line previously reported on “The Kinematics Of Doubt” in Implant sets 15th album ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ for 30 October on Alfa Matrix. The fourteen-track album is issued on CD and digital and includes “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” alongside “The Observer Effect,” “Underneath The Neon Lights,” “Pills,” “Civilization,” “Sanity,” “Framed,” “Transaction Failure,” “Are You Crying?,” “Talking In Your Sleep,” “Beyond The Code,” “No Apologies Required,” “On TV” and “Wounds.” Implant and Llumen launch their respective albums together on November 20, 2026 at mOtown in Sint-Joost-ten-Node, Belgium. About Implant Implant is the electro-industrial project Len Lemeire started in Belgium in 1996. The debut CD single, “Fun,” credited to Lemeire alongside Geert Machtelinck, was pressed in a numbered edition of 1,000 copies that year. The project’s catalogue spans harsh EBM, industrial dance, electro-pop and dark synth across releases including “Implantology,” “Audio Blender,” “The Productive Citizen” and the EP “Fading Away,” closing most releases with the line “Did you have your Implant today?” Implant released the free download single “The Drive” in December 2023. The twelfth studio album, “The Chaos Machines Part 1 – No More Flies On The Windscreen,” followed in May 2024. Lemeire discussed its modular-synth approach and a duet with Noemi Aurora in Implant interview: ‘Embrace chaos through the machines!’. The trilogy continued with the limited vinyl EP “The Chaos Machines Part 2 – Scratching The Surface” in September 2024 and closed with the album “Judging Sinners – The Chaos Machines Part 3” on February 7, 2025, again featuring Noemi Aurora and covered in Exclusive interview with Implant judging all those sinners. “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” Implant’s fifteenth studio album, follows on October 30, 2026. “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed,” out now as an eight-track EP, is the second single revealed from the record. items.body: A Faustian bargain begins with the ancient human suspicion that the universe can be persuaded to overlook consequence. We trade tomorrow for today, permanence for appetite, conscience for advantage, imagining that the account will somehow remain unsettled. Yet nature keeps exquisite books. Every shortcut alters the road; every borrowed fire casts its own darkness. The tragedy is seldom that we receive nothing for the price. Quite often, we receive precisely what we asked for. Power, knowledge, youth, wealth: these may all arrive intact. The horror lies in discovering, only afterward, that possession and fulfillment were never the same thing. Las Vegas has always been a fitting place for bad bargains. Money changes hands beneath artificial stars, luck is treated as a temporary religion, and every promise of sudden fortune carries an unspoken question about what somebody might surrender to obtain it. In the video for And It Was Night’s The Fever, composer and sound designer Rani Sharone turns that temptation into a compact morality play, casting himself as both gambler and Devil while an obsession gradually takes possession of the room. Inspired by the Twilight Zone episode of the same name, The Fever takes the old Faustian bargain and filters it through addiction. Sharone’s gambler appears trapped between appetite and consequence, surrounded by projected animation, theatrical props, and backgrounds that continually push the setting away from ordinary reality. The imagery works particularly well with the song’s dark electro-pop foundation, where Depeche Mode, Danny Elfman, The Cure, and Nick Cave provide useful coordinates without swallowing Sharone’s own identity. He calls the result “Dark Noir Pop,” an apt description for music that feels equally suited to a nightclub, a crooked casino, and the closing credits of some lost supernatural thriller. The Devil, naturally, has the easier job. Temptation requires charm before punishment enters the picture, and Sharone plays both sides of that transaction with an appropriately theatrical touch. By reducing the production to two characters embodied by one performer, the video turns its budgetary limitations into part of its psychological logic. Gambler and tempter begin to resemble two expressions of the same compulsion. “I didn’t want to do a literal retelling of the Twilight Zone episode the song was based off of,” says Sharone. “For practical reasons and budgetary/production limitations I chose to create something that I could pull off with a very limited crew and budget. The result ended up being me playing both characters, the gambler and devil, and shooting in front of custom commissioned animated projections to set the stage with props to make it as theatrical as I could to sell the story. I used a couple iconic horror sources to direct and inspire my visual FX supervisor when creating the background designs. Namely from The Shining. which inspired the look of the hotel room the gambler is in, and a couple visual cues from Creepshow for the more surreal background designs. Those with a keen eye will recognize them.” Watch the video for The Fever below: That horror lineage suits Sharone, whose résumé ranges from Puscifer and Stolen Babies to orchestral work performed by Hilary Hahn and recent contributions to the music team behind K-Pop Demon Hunters. With The Fever, his return to writing his own songs feels especially pointed: desire becomes addiction, luck becomes captivity, and the Devil barely needs to cheat. The gambler has already brought his weakness to the table. Sharone’s casino nightmare will also find an audience in Los Angeles tonight, Friday, October 2, when The Fever screens at El Cid as part of a monthly screening with a suitably spooky selection. Doors open at 7 p.m., with the screening beginning at 8 p.m.—another opportunity to watch the gambler discover exactly how much his good fortune costs. items.body: Rosetta Stone Executing Nostalgia Cleopatra Records Despite Porl King’s formal reactivation of the Rosetta Stone name happening a full seven years ago, it’s been remarkably tricky to pin down a specific sound or approach which has defined this era of King’s work. There have been reappraisals of interregnum work under the miserylab handle, syntheses of classic Rosetta Stone songwriting and modern production, and a suite of covers delivered with characteristic dryness which blurs the line between irony and earnestness. New release Executing Nostalgia embraces this amorphous fluidity, jamming all of King’s angles on goth rock into a dense forty minute listen. Without meaning to play armchair psychologist, I’d credit much of this restlessness to the question of King squaring the large bodies of work he recorded under the miserylab and Death It Ends from 2007 to 2018 with the idea of a “return” to Rosetta Stone. The legacy of In Death It Ends in particular may have been the key all along; from the moment a mesh of misty distorted guitar miasma joins the weighty, doomily reverbed bass and resigned, muttering vocals of opener “Shadowban”, that project’s unmistakable mix of classic darkwave and witchhouse is conjured up. There it remains for the remainder of the A-side of original material, mixed into spindly early Sisters fog machine goth on “Someone”, blended with miserylab minimalism on “Regression”, and compounded upon itself on the Soft Moon-like echoes of “Negative”. On the flip side, a set of five covers also sounds well-integrated and cooked down. Earlier tributes (“The Witch”, “Sisters Are Doing It For Themselves”) hinged upon deft yet tongue slightly in cheek elevations of naff source material to Rosetta Stone’s original, ornately stormy sound, but in choosing a set of ur-goth and relatedly dark tracks for Executing Nostalgia‘s back half, that issue vanishes. These are clearly tunes which helped shape King’s youthful tastes, and whether it’s the tempestuous “Incubus Succubus”, the high camp of the Prunes’ “Pagan Love Song”, or the sly shadowcraft of Colin Newman’s oft-overlooked “Alone”, they’re delivered forthrightly. From a purely musical perspective at this point in the Rosetta Stone reboot, opting to close the record with the looping, machine-like rhythmic punch of The Lorries’ “Talk About The Weather” is a subtle masterstroke. Partially made up of the sort of sparse clatter and jangle associated with miserylab but shot through with the sort of impassioned vocal vitriol which illuminated early Rosetta Stone material and the right winding guitar to suit, King’s version is almost slavishly true to the original, yet in that manner it draws together just about all the corners of his various epochs, a fitting marker of Rebooting Nostalgia‘s everything and the kitchen sink approach. Buy it. Executing Nostalgia by Rosetta Stone The post Rosetta Stone, “Executing Nostalgia” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Porl King在重启Rosetta Stone项目后的新作，将他多年来在不同子项目中的探索整合进约四十分钟的哥特摇滚框架中。专辑A面为原创作品，融合了darkwave、witchhouse以及minimalist等多种元素，吉他音色笼罩在浓雾般的失真中，贝斯线沉重而回响深广，人声疏离低语。B面为五首翻唱，选取了多首对King音乐品味有深远影响的ur-goth经典曲目，包括Incubus Succubus、Prunes的Pagan Love Song、Colin Newman的Alone以及The Lorries的Talk About The Weather。这些翻唱摒弃了早期作品中的戏谑感，以更为真挚直接的方式呈现。最后一曲对The Lorries的翻唱尤其巧妙，将miserylab时期的稀疏节奏与早期Rosetta Stone的强烈人声表现力融为一体，成为整张专辑各阶段创作脉络的总结标记。

items.excerpt: 京都を拠点とするバンドの、久保田麻琴プロデュースによる3作目。鴨川に架かる橋の数え歌“鴨ノ橋”が生むサイケでディープな音の渦に飲み込まれたかと思えば、サックスが咆哮するガレージ・ロック、ブギウギ調のウィード・ソング、レイドバックしたソウル風ナンバーと続き、尋常ではないエネルギーと尖った感性が発揮されている。“鴨ノ橋”のトランシーなリミックスも強烈!

items._genre: psychedelic rock / garage rock / soul / electronic remix
items._cn_summary: 京都乐队FRYING DUTCHMAN第三张专辑由久保田麻琴担任制作人，展现出旺盛的创作能量。专辑以鸭川桥梁为主题的曲目"鴨ノ橋"开场，编织出迷幻而深沉的音景漩涡，随后延伸至萨克斯咆哮的车库摇滚、布吉摇摆风格曲目以及放克灵魂乐，风格跨度极大。久保田麻琴的制作手法为专辑注入了尖锐的实验感，"鴨ノ橋"的恍惚迷幻重混版本以强烈的电子处理延续了开场曲目营造的沉浸氛围。整张专辑在风格边界间跳跃频繁，既有摇滚的原始张力，也融合了放克律动与电子实验处理，制作层面体现出明确的艺术导向。

items._cn_summary: 洛杉矶艺术家茱莉亚·霍尔特的新专辑定位为2024年《Something In The Room She Moves》的扩展性姊妹篇，以亲密的室内氛围为核心。编曲大量采用室内乐式配置，乐器编排具有古典质感，文本简洁，篇幅有限但聚焦于一张以梦幻氛围著称的单曲。整体风格偏向低限、慢速、私密的人声与器乐结合，与Cocteau Twins的漂浮质感有可比性。专辑延续了霍尔特一贯的文学性文本与精致制作路线，适合在安静的夜晚聆听。
