items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源自爱丁堡皇家植物园艺术家驻留项目，以园中最古老的萨巴尔棕榈树被砍伐为创作起点。声音设计师与作曲家Pippa Murphy合作，钢琴家Dave Milligan担任伴奏，以人声与钢琴为核心，辅以精细的声景设计。歌词与旋律中反复出现的短语作为记忆锚点，形成层层呼应的结构。专辑、舞台剧与书籍三位一体，讲述这棵棕榈树被发现实际为墨西哥萨巴尔品种的历史故事。音乐风格朴素而深沉，融合苏格兰民谣根基与当代作曲手法，配合warm的人声与节制的声音设计，营造出沉思而亲密的氛围。这是一部关于自然、历史与传承的安魂曲，也是一份对未来的希望寄语。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. Tako Toki - Un Dimanche � Monaco (Review) GuldGanger - GuldGanger (Review)

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以乌克兰传统民歌为根基，混合原创作品，聚焦于被俄罗斯强制迁徙的两万名乌克兰儿童的沉重主题。核心创作者Marichka是乌克兰裔加拿大歌手，她组织了两个音乐团体：一个位于乌克兰，另一个为全女性加拿大合唱团Daughters of Donbas。乐器编制以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉琴、钢琴，还使用了双陶笛独奏。演唱风格在不同曲目间形成鲜明对比：部分曲目以Marichka柔和的声线演绎传统叙事歌曲的哀伤情感，另一些曲目则由Alina Kuzma以激烈粗粝的方式诠释与自然精灵相关的仪式歌曲。专辑将历史题材与当代地缘政治悲剧编织在一起，传统旋律成为承载记忆与控诉的载体。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._genre: afro-funk / vodun music / afro-cuban fusion / benin groove
items._cn_summary: Analog Africa 厂牌再版贝宁传奇乐队 Orchestre Poly-Rythmo 与歌手 Antoine Dougbé 于 1977 至 1982 年间的合作录音。Dougbé 被称作"魔鬼首相"，以 Vodun 信仰为创作根基，独创以拍腿节奏 Cavacha 为核心的音乐传递方式。该节奏源自鼓手 Belobi Meridjo 从火车节奏中提取的律动，后广泛渗透至七十年代中期的刚果流行音乐。专辑横跨 1970 年代末至 80 年代初，音色呈现时代特征——吉他带有塑料光泽感，合成器开始介入编排，但整体律动仍根植于 70 年代传统。古巴 son 元素在开篇曲目中尤为突出，刚果伦巴的影响也清晰可辨。曲目如《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺底，闪烁吉他与高帽密集律动交织，吉他声部在中段分裂展开，再由合成器织回底层。《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》则更直接地展现古巴印记，持续牛铃、鼻音浓郁的应答式人声与紧密重复的吉他律动构成骨架。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手兼音乐档案学者Dominique Cravic与地下漫画家Robert Crumb联合的Les Primitifs du futur乐队录制，是他们的第五张作品。乐队在巴黎咖啡馆相遇后开始合作，专辑以Crumb的封面插画为标志。音乐融合了手风琴主导的bal-musette风格，同时纳入拉格泰姆、jug乐队、法国香颂、skiffle等多种被边缘化的传统风格，使用从老唱片中挖掘的曲目加以重新编排。器乐编制极其丰富，包括手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等。Cravic的演唱方式接近Maurice Chevalier式的口语化叙事。专辑收录了向2020年去世的法国抵抗运动传奇歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的作品，以及对Bette Midler、Bing Crosby等人曾演绎过的老歌的重新诠释。整体定位为对被遗忘音乐传统的考古式复兴，演奏严肃且充满热情。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣界资深歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔，收录五首曲目，多为传统音乐改编。整体营造出一种古老而略带粗粝的氛围，骑乘般律动的开场曲《Svennedal》充分展示了主唱富有说服力的嗓音；《Nordgård》是乐队成员唯一的原创作品，以口琴与风笛推动节奏；传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》中扬琴为背景增添细腻层次；终曲《Ormsö》为器乐曲，口琴与长笛、弦乐交织出富有弹性的奇特声响。整张EP呈现出超越新人水准的成熟度，乐评对其完整专辑充满期待。

items.body: Deathrock has always had a practical relationship with bad news. A macabre sense of mortality supplies the subject matter, punk supplies the impatience, and everyday life keeps renewing the subscription. East Bay four-piece Normal Weirds bring those concerns together on Frown Time, a title that sounds reasonably restrained given the circumstances. Released October 2, the band’s second full-length gathers ten songs that push further into deathpunk and deathrock while retaining their anarcho-punk roots and post-punk unease. The band’s own description, “deathrock gloom dragged through the dirt of punk,” gives a useful indication of the record’s priorities: atmosphere, abrasion, and the urgency of having something unpleasant to get off your chest. Normal Weirds released their debut album, Same Difference, in 2024, followed by the six-song EP No Lease On Life in 2025. The debut examined growing up and working free of the circumstances that had already laid out a person’s future. Taken alongside that earlier record, Frown Time suggests a widening field of concern, with individual frustration meeting the larger sense that the whole arrangement is becoming increasingly fucked. Driving basslines and hard, direct drums provide the foundation, with guitars moving between wiry punk attack and darker passages thickened by effects. Urgent, sometimes theatrical vocals heighten the unease, while lean arrangements preserve the roughness of the band’s approach. The emphasis stays on noise, tension, and the force of the playing, giving their darker direction a distinctly physical edge. The band offers Rudimentary Peni, Cemetery, T.S.O.L., and Chain Cult as points of comparison. “Deathpunk” feels like a useful shorthand for the territory they describe, where punk aggression and deathrock atmosphere share the same cramped quarters. Across their releases, Normal Weirds have increasingly brought those impulses together, giving the darker material a harder and more direct frame. Mortality, alienation, and everyday absurdity run through the album’s lyrical concerns. Its ominous mood draws on both personal experience and a broader disillusionment with the present. There is a bluntness to the title that suits that outlook: Frown Time makes room for the irritation and apprehension people are often expected to swallow while getting on with their day. Frown Time was recorded, mixed, and produced by Skot Brown of Altar De Fey and mastered by Greg Wilkinson. The album is available to stream and purchase on Bandcamp here. It will be released on other streaming platforms, excluding Spotify, on October 16, 2026. Listen to Frown Time below: Frown Time by Normal Weirds Follow Normal Weirds: Instagram Facebook YouTube Bandcamp Linktree The post East Bay Deathpunks Normal Weirds Stare Down Mortality on New Album “Frown Time” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Normal Weirds 的第二张全长专辑延续了乐队对死亡摇滚与硬核朋克融合的探索，专辑收录十首作品，将阴郁氛围与朋克攻击性压缩在紧凑的框架内。贝斯线条主导推进，鼓点硬朗直接，吉他游走于尖锐的朋克冲击与效果器加厚的暗黑段落之间。人声时而急促、时而戏剧化，配合简洁的编曲保留了粗糙的质地。歌词围绕死亡、异化与日常荒诞展开，既有个人经验也有对当下环境的幻灭感。专辑由 Skot Brown 录制并混音，Greg Wilkinson 负责母带处理，制作保持了乐队的原始张力，是一张将死亡摇滚气质推得更硬、更直接的延续性作品。

items._cn_summary: 这是The Wire电台节目的曲目单汇总，涵盖十数位艺术家的单曲与专辑片段，横跨自由即兴、噪音、电子、实验人声和当代器乐等领域。选曲来自相对唱片、Profound Lore、Horror Vector、Constellation Tatsu等独立与小众厂牌，整体偏向地下实验场景。Don Cherry的现场录音呈现七十年代自由爵士脉络，Brandon Seabrook延续前卫吉他即兴传统，Agnes Haus与Kukangendai提供极简抽象的器乐文本，Ghost Dubs与Ziùr则将电子节拍与质感噪音作为主线。Krallice等金属乐队作品以极端化的技术处理介入节目，展示了噪音摇滚与前卫金属在实验语境下的渗透。作为节目预告性质的内容，该文本不具备深度评论属性，更像是电台DJ的选曲清单，用以呈现当下国际实验音乐的多样面貌。

items._cn_summary: 挪威创作歌手苏珊娜·桑福的最新专辑仅以人声与管风琴在教堂中录制，向十四世纪英国神秘主义者朱利安之作致敬。受近期为人母的经历启发，专辑围绕宗教文本展开，在空旷教堂的声学环境中捕捉纯粹的声学质感。桑福虽以实验与电子元素闻名，但此次刻意回归最简编制，呈现出庄严与内省的聆听氛围。评论指出她即便在最克制、最实验的状态下，依然能以独特的个人风格创造亲和力强的音乐。这张作品与其以往风格形成鲜明对照，是对声学空间、古代文本与极简美学的探索。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Pekka Streng's music is colored by his personal history, much like the stories of Tim Buckley or Nick Drake, singer-songwriters who passed away prematurely. Perhaps unconsciously, they gravitated toward that deeply intimate, heart-wrenching subgenre, the folk singer-songwriter, in which an artist reveals so much of themselves. He was accompanied by musicians from the Finnish jazz scene, such as Eero Koivistoinen and Pekka P�yry (on saxophone and flute, respectively); both would later participate in bassist Pekka Pohjola's album Harakka Bialoipokku (1974)."Mimosaneito" ventures into jazz, yet the mood shifts to something more intimate and reflective on "Kaukana." Pekka possessed the power to transport us out of our reality through the sheer magic of his vocal timbre; like singer-songwriters such as Donovan, he commanded a rich stylistic range, shifting between psychedelic, acoustic, jazz-inflected, and ethereal sounds, to enter that mythological realm which, at times during the 60s and 70s, felt so real it was almost tangible.From the groove-laden pop of the track ...Ja Tuittu Ruusut Sai to a blues piece with a touch of rustic country in Perhonen. However, it was Pekka's more mystical, mysterious, and inspired side that truly shone when he sang in Finnish, performing tracks like Auringon Lapsi that evoked distant, almost medieval, times, as if they had reached us through oral tradition. It was also reminiscent of the early days of Tyrannosaurus Rex, when Marc Bolan favored an acoustic sound and explored Eastern and psychedelic influences.As for the title, it alludes to the land in summer, when everything bursts into color and blooms; the summer solstice is precisely when Juhannus is celebrated in Finland, a time when people traditionally headed to the lakes throughout June. Both the cover art and the music convey something of this spirit. It ranges from a dark organ solo on "Kanttorinpoika Max" to the magical "Katsele Y�ss�," featuring only Pekka's voice, his guitar, and a rather Baroque-style sopranino saxophone solo.Roope Hattu reminded me of the freshness and freedom of Bob Dylan's bluesy "The Man in Me", though this was the Finnish version, transformed by Jukka Ruohom�ki's synthesizers into a kind of cosmic blues, evolving from the style of The Band (Dylan's friends and collaborators) into something otherworldly. "Puutarhassa" sports a very welcome bossa nova vibe that lends itself well to the acoustic format and the album's stylistic, and emotional, variety, shifting from the optimism of a sunny day... to the introspection of a gray, rainy one, if we are talking about stereotypes, that is. Though certainly not musical ones."Mutta Min� L�hden" is curiously divided into two parts: one acoustic, featuring guitar, and another with vocals and the celesta, that instrument created by the French harmonium maker Auguste Mustel. Resembling a glockenspiel, it takes us by surprise not only with its sweetness but also with its brevity; it is a piece filled with ambivalence, yet one that leaves us certain we have heard a genuine expression of the artist's own voice.

items._cn_summary: 这张1972年的芬兰专辑将民谣创作置于北欧夏至的文化语境中，融合爵士乐手参与编排，呈现从巴洛克式高音萨克斯独奏、bossa nova律动到原声内省的多元面貌。曲目在迷幻民谣、布鲁斯、乡村元素与芬兰语演唱的神秘气质间游走，合成器的加入带来某种宇宙感。乐评指出Pekka Streng的嗓音具有将听众带入另一时空的能力，其作品与Tim Buckley、Nick Drake、Marc Bolan早期Tyrannosaurus Rex的私密风格相呼应。专辑将芬兰夏天的自然意象与中世纪口传传统质感结合，封面与音乐共同传达这一精神。然而整体仍以传统民谣创作为核心，实验性与前卫程度有限，对追求极端实验或即兴的听众而言偏保守，但在北欧民谣融合爵士与迷幻的维度上具有独到价值。

items.body: Sevit released “Requiem”, a darkwave album the Dallas-area duo wrote as the follow-up to 2021’s “On The Edge Of A Darker Place,” on 1 October 2026. The nine-track record sat unfinished for years, surfacing only after a self-titled Sevit album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” runs nine tracks: Ode To A Requiem Beyond My Control Escape Dreamland In So Many Words It Must Be Berlin Until Sundown The Happy Crowd The Walls Are Closing In (Original Version) Requiem Requiem by Sevit Sevit have not detailed why the record was set aside, but the band summed up the gap in one line: “Maybe some records simply have to wait until the people who created them finally catch up with them.” Sevit’s ‘Requiem’ follows ‘On The Edge Of A Darker Place’ “Requiem” is out now on Bandcamp as a digital release. About Sevit Jackie Legos (vocals, guitar) and Cam B. (synths, programming) write and record Sevit from the Dallas, Texas area, where the duo formed in 2020 after both had played in earlier North Texas bands, including At Night and Pleasure Crisis. They issued the “A Darker Place” EP that same year and signed to Peru’s InClub Records that October. Sevit’s debut album, “On The Edge Of A Darker Place,” arrived in September 2021: thirteen tracks that draw on The Cure, Joy Division, Bauhaus and Siouxsie & The Banshees, played live by a five-piece band built around the Legos and Cam B. core. Jackie Legos has described the band’s lyrics as rooted in “poetry, and things that might have directly and indirectly crossed my path in life.” The duo wrote “Requiem” as that album’s direct sequel, then set it aside. A self-titled album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” finally surfaces, closing a chapter the band had otherwise left open.
items._cn_summary: Sevit由来自德州达拉斯的双人组Jackie Legos与Cam B.组成，2020年成军后延续了The Cure、Joy Division、Bauhaus与Siouxsie & The Banshees等经典乐队的影响。《Requiem》原是2021年专辑《On The Edge Of A Darker Place》的直接续作，但因故搁置数年，直到2024年同名专辑填补空缺后才于2026年10月正式发行。九首曲目以低沉人声与合成器编程为骨架，歌词根植于诗歌与个人经历。整张专辑仅以数字形式通过Bandcamp发行，缺乏厂牌背景与实验突破的描述，乐评本身也更接近新闻通稿而非深度评论。

items.body: The Pixel Rain released “Glitching Sky” on October 2, 2026, the fourth and final advance single from the Southeast London act’s debut album, “A Sense of Danger,” due October 29 on Bandcamp, Spotify and other digital platforms. The track pushes vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler’s electronic side further forward, bringing futurepop and synthwave into the project’s established synthpop sound, with Siegler citing VNV Nation and Chvrches among the single’s reference points. At the center of the song is a character retreating from an unfulfilling reality into a virtual world where he can construct a more powerful version of himself. Siegler extends the idea beyond any specific technology or platform to a broader comment on how people seek distraction from anxiety, disappointment and everyday life. Siegler describes the retreat as carrying both sadness and absurdity: “The idea came from thinking about someone whose real life isn’t giving them very much, so they retreat into a virtual world where they can be whoever they want to be. There’s something quite sad about that, but also something a little ridiculous, so I wanted the story to have both sides to it. “I deliberately left the virtual world undefined because I think that kind of escape can take a lot of different forms. I’m certainly not outside of it myself. We all have things we disappear into when reality gets uncomfortable. “The music is quite fast and energetic, but the song itself takes its time building. That seemed to fit the idea: you don’t necessarily notice yourself getting drawn further and further into these little distractions until they’ve started taking up much more of your life than you intended.” The single arrives with a visualizer by Sophie Maria Vickers, built around the song’s virtual setting and digital imagery. Glitching Sky by The Pixel Rain On Bandcamp, “Glitching Sky” is bundled together with The Pixel Rain’s three earlier advance singles, “Last,” “A Sense of Danger” and “Sacrifice.” The single is also on Spotify and other major platforms. About The Pixel Rain The Pixel Rain is the solo project of vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler, originally from Hungary and now based in Southeast London. The project emerged from London’s underground scene with a self-titled debut EP in 2023, and mixes dark electronic and post-punk elements with guitar, electronics and industrial textures. The Pixel Rain released the first single from its forthcoming debut album, “Last,” on June 19, 2026, with a video shot in Hungary in which Siegler was joined on screen by Balázs Fűr, András Melles, Máté Breier and Máté Király-Gyeőry. The singles “A Sense of Danger” and “Sacrifice” followed over the summer, each previewing the album further. “Glitching Sky,” released October 2, 2026, is the fourth and final advance single before the debut album “A Sense of Danger” arrives on October 29, 2026. The album explores power, authority, consumerism and social unease through recurring post-apocalyptic and technological imagery.
items._cn_summary: The Pixel Rain是常驻伦敦的匈牙利裔音乐人Áron Siegler的独立项目，融合暗潮电子、后朋克、工业质感与吉他元素。即将发行的首张专辑《A Sense of Danger》以单曲《Glitching Sky》先行释出，该曲在既定合成器流行基础上引入futurepop与synthwave色彩。歌曲讲述角色逃离现实、在虚拟世界中构建理想化自我，借此反思当代人借由各种逃避机制消解焦虑与失望的普遍现象。编曲快节奏且能量充沛，但结构上缓慢铺陈，呼应主题中人不知不觉越陷越深的状态。作为独立厂牌发行的小众作品，文本来源偏新闻通稿性质，缺少深入的音乐分析。整体呈现具有一定艺术构思的合成器流行，融合暗潮与后朋克的氛围构建，作为新人作品展现出对逃避主义议题的个人化表达。

items.body: Town And Towers Records has signed Swiss duo CØLDSTAR, releasing the band’s new single “Last Night On Earth” on 2 October 2026. The track is the Bern-based darkwave, synthpop and coldwave act’s first release on the Danish label. “Last Night On Earth” follows a narrator watching Earth’s final hours from roughly seven hundred miles above the planet, aboard a spacecraft where the oxygen cycles mechanically and the view of the dying world shrinks to a reflection in glass. The lyrics state the moment directly: “The blue marble fades in a rear view of glass / I watch from the silence as centuries pass.” There is no rescue attempt in the story and no final message, only “a velvet curtain, and we’re not coming back.” Dark synth layers, pulsing electronic rhythms and melancholic melodies carry the track’s icy, futuristic atmosphere. Town And Towers names VNV Nation and Black Nail Cabaret as reference points for that sound. Recommend to fans of Solar Fake, Final Selection, Depeche Mode, Covenant and The Soft Moon. CØLDSTAR’s ‘Last Night On Earth’ is the duo’s first release for Town And Towers Records “Last Night On Earth” is out now as a digital single, also streaming via Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, SoundCloud and Tidal. Last Night On Earth by CØLDSTAR Town And Towers Records’ recent roster also includes deZeption, signed in 2024, and Hatif, whose album “Small States” arrived via the label in 2025. About CØLDSTAR Martin Baumann and Michael Freund record as CØLDSTAR from Bern, Switzerland, mixing darkwave, synthpop, coldwave and retro-futurist synth sounds. The duo’s songs use space and science-fiction imagery to address isolation, memory, technology, longing and human existence. CØLDSTAR’s early releases included a 2021 cover of Nine Inch Nails‘ “Hurt.” The band built out its own catalogue with the “Coming Home” EP in 2023, then the debut album “CØSMIC DUST” in 2024 via Swiss Dark Nights, combining atmospheric electronics, synthpop melody and darker post-punk influences. Singles “Time Machine,” “Astronaut’s Lament,” “Last Dance” and “Post-Punk Robot” followed. “Post-Punk Robot” reached number 2 on the Deutsche Alternative Charts in 2026. “Last Night On Earth” is the fifth single CØLDSTAR has issued since “CØSMIC DUST,” and the first through Town And Towers Records.
items._cn_summary: 瑞士双人组CØLDSTAR签约丹麦厂牌Town And Towers Records，发布单曲《Last Night On Earth》。歌曲以太空叙事为框架，叙述者从距地面约七百英里的飞船上观看地球最后的时刻，没有救援，只有沉默的告别。黑暗合成器层次、脉冲式电子节拍与忧郁旋律构建出冰冷而未来感的氛围。乐队此前已在Swiss Dark Nights发行首张专辑《CØLMIC DUST》，单曲《Post-Punk Robot》曾登上德国另类榜单第二名。该作品在暗潮与合成器流行类型内呈现出成熟的制作水准，但整体仍属于类型化框架内的常规表达，未见显著的实验性突破或跨领域融合尝试。

items.body: Death Strip release their fourth single, “Flash Back,” on October 8, 2026. The duo mixes darkwave and EBM with an electro-punk edge. “Flash Back” runs at 136 BPM, built on distorted saw bass, strobing arpeggios and deadpan spoken word. Recommend to fans of Boy Harsher, Gesaffelstein and The Prodigy. The single is scheduled to land on Death Strip’s Bandcamp and Spotify pages on release day. About Death Strip Death Strip pairs Jonas Moberg, a Swedish producer and drummer based on Gotland, with vocalist Culture Yob, also known as Son of Daughter, based in Hastings, England. Moberg played drums in the Swedish rock band Jumper, which released three albums and eleven singles between 1996 and 2000, and later played live drums for Paloma Faith early in her career. Culture Yob co-founded the band Gobsausage with Takalina and Miss Halski in the early 2000s, and also co-founded Charles of London, according to the band. The two met in the 2000s and lived in neighboring warehouse flats in Shoreditch, London, where they shared a goods lift. They now live apart, Moberg on Gotland and Culture Yob in Hastings, and write and record Death Strip’s music remotely. The two have never been in the same room for a Death Strip session. “Flash Back,” released October 8, 2026, is the fourth single Death Strip has made this way.
items._cn_summary: Death Strip 是一支由瑞典制作人 Jonas Moberg 与英国 vocalist Culture Yob 组成的远程合作二人组，第四支单曲《Flash Back》定于 2026 年 10 月 8 日发行。整首作品建立在 136 BPM 的节奏之上，以失真锯齿波贝斯、频闪式琶音与冷调念白为骨架，将暗潮、EBM 与 electro-punk 的攻击性融为一炉。两位成员虽在 2000 年代于伦敦 Shoreditch 同一栋仓库相识，却从未在同一房间内录音，所有编曲、拍摄均以数字方式异地协作完成。推荐给 Gesaffelstein、The Prodigy 与 Boy Harsher 的听众。整体呈现更接近新闻发布而非评论，信息相对简短，对声音设计的深度描述有限。

items.body: What’s old is always new again. We got a full-blown nü metal revival on our hands, noise rock is arguably as popular as it’s ever been, and Myspace-era metalcore is getting about as many new releases from bands with members who were born around the same time the legends were laying the foundation. I was also recently reminded that fucking Greta Van Fleet exists for some godforsaken reason. For some other reason, I feel like we’ve just kinda skipped over a lot of good stuff. Where’s the grunge revival? Where’s the college-rock revival? Where’s the early post-punk revival? Where’s all the shit that sounds like it was made by people who hadn’t yet figured out what genre they were supposed to be in? Why does everyone nowadays sound so ready to be categorized?Well, Whippets make a case to step into these shoes, sounding something like Unwound by way of Dinosaur Jr. and Jay Reatard, or like Fugazi covering Dismemberment Plan and Siouxsie and the Banshees at the same time. They convey this volatile energy with writhing guitar leads that are often as eerie as they are anthemic, and tuneful bass in a rhythm section that paves the way for both their most unruly and airy moments. Much like their 2024 self-titled release, Whippets again flex their knack for melodies that get their hooks in your eardrums like velcro. No Skulls is every bit as fearless and without boundaries, gaining traction across a multitude of late 80s and early 90s soundscapes, regularly finding familiar touchpoints with the intuition to pull the rug at just the right time, or mix ‘n’ match influences in a way that’s as much “Aha!” as it is “What the fuck?” It’s like post-punk found the perfectly imperfect dancing partner in shoegaze, distraught while still finding an endearing footing, abrasive, oddly charming, and eyebrow-raising all at once.The video for album opener “These Woods” taps into a similar throwback, like it could’ve been dug out of a shoebox full of forgotten tapes and old zines. With a hazy camcorder look, sunbleached and spliced together with live footage, BMXers, scrapbook imagery, and other ’90s feels, it has the scrappy and surreal feel of something you might’ve stumbled across on MTV’s 120 Minutes at 1 a.m. It’s an appropriate visual companion, familiar enough to trigger a deeply buried memory, but weird enough to feel like you’ve never quite seen it before—and maybe even inspire a bad haircut.Check it out: No Skulls drops today, October 2, on wax and digital via No Coast Records.

items._cn_summary: Whippets 乐队新专辑《No Skulls》被置于近年怀旧风潮的背景下进行审视，乐评指出他们填补了硬核复兴热潮中常被忽视的空白——即对早期后朋克、垃圾摇滚与独立摇滚黄金年代的回望。作品被比作 Unwound 与 Dinosaur Jr. 的混合体，借鉴 Fugazi、Dismemberment Plan 与 Siouxsie and the Banshees 的影响，在八九十年代各种声音景观间自由穿梭。乐评特别强调其旋律的侵略性，吉他主音兼具诡异与朗朗上口的气质，节奏组支撑起躁动与空灵的双重张力。同名专辑中的钩子旋律在此延续，并展现出混搭影响的手法和令人意外的转折。配套 MV 采用九十年代家庭录像质感，与音乐气质高度契合。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴家 Maria Kalaniemi 与钢琴家 Timo Alakotila 合作逾三十五年，二人以北欧民谣为基底展开亲密的器乐对话。专辑多为二人编制，搭配 Kalaniemi 无歌词的人声吟唱与少量弦乐四重奏，呈现宁静、绵长、如梦似幻的呼吸感。他们既演奏斯堪的纳维亚传统曲目（如开场曲《Lyckänskan》），也加入原创作品与一首 Piazzolla《Oblivion》以及芬兰式探戈。演奏重心放在旋律本身与即兴流动上，而非炫技，整体克制内敛，适合安静聆听。作为世界音乐分支的北欧民谣，它与用户偏好的实验、电子、暗潮等方向距离较远，但其细腻的器乐编排与文化地域性仍具一定审美价值。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John 1999年在德国Loreley露天剧场的演出，由WDR电视台的Rockpalast节目录制发行。乐队由吉他手Bobby Broom、贝斯手David Barard和鼓手Herman Ernest组成，是一支紧凑有力的新奥尔良四人组。演出曲目涵盖新奥尔良经典如《Iko, Iko》，以及Dr. John本人的代表作如《I Walk on Guilded Splinters》《Right Place, Wrong Time》和《Big Chief》，还向Duke Ellington致敬。乐评将Loreley的传说氛围与Dr. John的神秘主义气质相联系，强调其Mardi Gras式的表演风格和对新奥尔良根源的延续。文章内容为乐评但文字似乎在结尾被截断，部分语句不完整。整体属于具有地域文化色彩的根源音乐演出，与实验或前卫领域距离较远。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / sound documentary
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区实地录制，二十余名枪支暴力亲历者在街头口述亲身经历，从十七岁到六十七岁不等。专辑没有任何配乐添加，仅收录了受访者的声音与周围环境音，包括摩托车声、蚊虫声以及米德威机场上空的飞机轰鸣。录制地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家的前廊，恰好在特朗普宣布派遣国民警卫队进入芝加哥的当天进行。项目收益将捐赠给反暴力组织Cure Violence Global。这并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是以声音为载体的社会纪实，将田野录音、口述历史与社会议题融为一体，形成一种介于实验声响与人类学档案之间的聆听体验。

items.body: Review by Lewian — It is somewhat frustrating about rock from the old communist GDR (East Germany) that the possibilityof censorship didn't only affect the lyrics but apparently also had an impact on the music itself.People were strongly discouraged to think outside the box, and also to sound outside the box. Soproper innovation was very hard to find if at all. Everyone apparently wanted to (or had to) soundnice and civilised. In the 70s it was possible to play harder rock music if it clearly referenced,copied or covered rock'n roll and blues from the west as this was seen as anti western establishmentrebellion and therefore OK (at least at a certain time point), but rebellion against the ownconditions of life in the east wasn't allowed. This also meant that anything more aggressive anddark couldn't be done in innovative ways and couldn't directly relate to the musicians' daily life,seriously affecting creativity. Any opposition had to be subtle, often covered by nice melodicmusic, often enough straight and easy to listen to, and often of little attraction to the proglistener 40 years or so later. Lyrics were often poetic and indirect. Innovation could be brought in best by incorporating classical musicinfluences, as Electra and Stern Meissen did, and Lift to some extent. I believe that the situationfor creativity was really more problematic in the GDR than it was for example in Poland, Hungary andthe Czech Republic, but I can't know for sure (certainly there was a more lively jazz scene in thelatter countries).Lift's Meeresfahrt is one of the best albums to negotiate these conditions. It is in factastonishing that the major theme of longing for travel and far away countries on this album didn'tcreate problems with the censors, as far as I know, given that most people were not allowed totravel outside the eastern communist block of countries. The album is very melodic indeed, the band doesn't rock hard (OK a little bit in very few places),but they are good at what they do. Most arrangements are dominated by the two very good keyboarders.The vocals are also attractive, clean and melodic. The opener "Wir fahrn uebers Meer" is an exampleof copying western blues rock. Maybe the band used this to distract the censors, because in my viewit is by far the weakest track. This is followed by the extremely beautiful "Nach Sueden" ("GoSouth"). Not the proggiest track, but featuring a wonderful melody, a strong keyboard part, andlyrics on migrating birds that probably expressed the longing of many young people in the GDR butwere seemingly (and surprisingly) innocent enough for the censors to let the band get away withthis. A highlight!"Scherbenglas" is an example for the classical influence, using only a string section and voice. Norock at all but interesting and not bad. "Tagesreise" has an epic melody and works well asrecommendation piece for the prog fan with some contrasts and several sections. The second highlightof the album.On the B-side, "Meeresfahrt" (something like "Journey at Sea") is the longest track. It developsslowly from calm keyboards into a mostly instrumental journey featuring the keyboarders andsaxophonist in particular. This is surely enjoyable even though it may be a bit too long for what itis. "Sommernacht" is a calm good night song referencing traditional singing. It works well asending, even though not very interesting from the instrumental point of view. "Tagesreise" and "Meeresfahrt" hold most interest from the prog point of view, but the album hasvery nice elements also elsewhere if you are into melodic rock. It has light influences fromclassical music, jazz and blues. It has good variety but also comes over as consistent featuring acharacteristic style, particularly the melodies and keyboards. The most similar band I can think of is Novalis. Personally I'd rank this as thesecond best GDR prog/art rock album (after Stern Meissen's Reise zum Mittelpunkt des Menschen). 3.7stars.Sadly, few months after the release of this album in 1978, band members Henry Pacholski and GerhardZachar died in a traffic accident and the band would never be the same anymore.

items.body: Review by Warthur — This is Jack Bruce's firet solo album, at least in terms of release date - the Things We Like jamsession was recorded prior to this and released as a follow-up. I've never fully gotten onboard withCream, and maybe it's Eric Clapton that's the component that doesn't quite land for me, becausebetween Ginger Baker's work elsewhere and now this I can say I'm more impressed with the other Creammembers' solo fare than Clapton's.What you get here is bluesy art rock with brilliant bass lines and poetic lyrics by Pete Brown. Somesongs on here ended up travelling widely, with Mountain, Colosseum, and Greenslade covering farelike Theme From An Imaginary Western or Rope Ladder To the Moon; others definitely qualify as deepcuts. Either way, well worth exploring.

items.body: Harry Birch wrote “Don’t Give Up” while he was drinking himself under and his mother was dying of bone cancer. “This song saved me,” he says. He wrote it for her. The music pulls against all that: warm bass, guitar ringing bright over it, the tempo unhurried. Only the first line gives it away, Birch calling himself “a whiskey walking junkie”. Halfway through the song, he hands a verse to Lunda, a French-Congolese singer working in soul and indie rock. The chorus asks for time to put a broken life back together: “Please don’t give up on me / ‘Cause oh on our love we can revive / the pieces of our life…” Birch is Kaya Street, the Bristol project he writes, sings and produces. He formed it in 2014 as a ten-piece soul band, broke it up in early 2024 to get into the studio properly, then rebuilt it at the end of that year around live horns, drums and electronics. Juno-winning Toronto producer Dubmatix is producing the next Kaya Street album. “Don’t Give Up” stands apart from the afrobeat he usually works in, and from the political songs that come with it. items.body: Disorder Festival, a new two-day event dedicated to the international goth, coldwave, darkwave, post-punk and EBM scenes, takes place in Montreuil, just outside Paris, on 6 and 7 February 2027. The festival spreads across four venues in the same neighbourhood instead of a single site: La Marbrerie, Le Chinois, Le Bal Chavaux and La Bicyclette. A further wave of artists is due to be revealed on 30 October. Some artists will be available for interviews, and press and photo accreditation can be arranged through the festival’s local PR, Take Me Out. About Disorder Festival Disorder is a new festival built around the international goth, coldwave, darkwave, post-punk and EBM scenes, set to debut in Montreuil on 6 and 7 February 2027. The organisers are spreading the event across four venues in the same part of Montreuil instead of concentrating it in one site: La Marbrerie, Le Chinois, Le Bal Chavaux and La Bicyclette. items.body: Vampire Valentine release “Scarred & Sacred” on October 25, 2026 via Morella Records. The six-track EP is the UK darkwave and post-punk trio’s fourth release since signing to the label on January 15, 2026, following a run of singles, the “Pale Dawn” EP and their self-titled debut album this past August. Where the self-titled album was a complete statement of the band’s sound, “Scarred & Sacred” follows a single arc across its six tracks: sin, repentance and the reckoning that waits at the gate. “Scarred & Sacred is our sins repenting and facing your fate in the afterlife at the gate,” the band says. “We wanted six tracks that felt like one story, not six songs that happened to ship together. It starts calm and it does not stay that way.” Scarred & Sacred tracklist Scarred (instrumental) – an atmospheric, melodic intro that turns unsettling, setting up the EP. Broken Sins – a full-length track pairing darkwave production with post-punk revival. Talisman – the story of a lover placing a talisman with a dying partner to guide them to the other side. Lover Not A Biter (instrumental) – a hard-driven darksynth track. GORE! (instrumental) – a darksynth cut the band describes as built on 1980s horror soundtracks and visuals. Sacred – the title track and closer, a post-punk song ending on vocals from frontman Michael Longstaff. Credits Michael Longstaff handles lyrics and vocals, Kieron Wright plays bass and Tobias Cowen Pickard plays drums. Tony Gunk produced, composed, mixed and mastered all six tracks. Ricky Conover, who records as Forerunnerx, co-produced and co-composed “Scarred”, “Lover Not A Biter” and “GORE!”. Blake Carpenter plays guitar on “Broken Sins”, “Talisman”, “Lover Not A Biter” and “GORE!”. About Vampire Valentine Vampire Valentine is a darkwave and post-punk band from Newcastle upon Tyne, formed in October 2025 by producer Michael Longstaff and bassist/guitarist Kieron Wright, who connected through a mutual acquaintance, along with drummer Tobias Cowen Pickard. US producers Ricky Conover (Forerunnerx) and Tony Gunk handle production. The band draws on The Sisters of Mercy, Twin Tribes, She Past Away and Lebanon Hanover. They debuted on November 14, 2025 with the single “Porcelain”, backed with “Olivia”, which goth journalist Mick Mercer called an “Excellent Debut”. A second single, “Thorns”, followed on December 1, 2025. Vampire Valentine signed to Morella Records on January 15, 2026 and released their debut full-length album that August, having already shared the singles “In The Dark” and “Cutting Ties” from it. “Scarred & Sacred”, out October 25, follows as the band’s fourth Morella release in under a year.
items._cn_summary: Vampire Valentine 是来自英国纽卡斯尔的暗潮与后朋克三人组，2026年通过 Morella Records 发行六曲EP《Scarred & Sacred》。整张作品围绕「罪、忏悔与彼岸清算」这一单一叙事弧展开，从氛围化的器乐前奏逐步推进至以darksynth驱动的硬节奏曲目，融合了1980年代恐怖电影配器的视觉化元素。主唱 Michael Longstaff 负责人声与歌词，低音与鼓机构成节奏骨架，吉他作为色彩层点缀其中。制作上由 Tony Gunk 主导，部分曲目与 Forerunnerx 联合制作，编曲层次清晰但风格框架仍属于暗潮类型内的常规操作。该EP延续了乐队对 Sisters of Mercy、Twin Tribes 等前辈的致敬路径，以主题统一性弥补了在声响探索方面的有限突破，适合偏好哥特复兴与暗潮叙事的听众，但对于追求实验性融合或独特声音设计的受众而言，提供的惊喜较为有限。

items.body: Assemblage 23 releases “Believe (INHALT Remix)” on 2 October 2026 via Metropolis Records. The single reworks “Believe”, the opening track from Tom Shear’s tenth Assemblage 23 album “Null”, released in November 2025. The remix comes from US producer Matia Simovich, who records as INHALT. “In INHALT’s expert hands, this song has been transformed. It has one foot on the mid-’80s dancefloor and the other planted firmly in the future,” Shear says of the rework. Believe (INHALT Remix) by Assemblage 23 “Believe” first appeared on “Null”, which Shear promoted with a UK tour ahead of its release and a run of sold-out shows in Germany. He returns to Europe this October for further dates in Germany and Sweden, several of which are already sold out. “‘Believe’ is about a hope for better things, even with the state of the world as it is today,” Shear said when the song first came out. “We are responsible for making the kind of world we live in. In the face of bad times, sometimes the most subversive thing you can do is to have hope.” Assemblage 23 live dates, October 2026 20 October – Karlsruhe, Die Stadtmitte (Germany) 21 October – Oberhausen, Kulttempel (Germany) 22 October – Hamburg, Indra Musikclub (Germany) 23 October – Jönköping, SekktorF (Sweden) – sold out 24 October – Hannover, Subkultur (Germany) – sold out Remaining tickets are available through the Assemblage 23 website. About Assemblage 23 Assemblage 23 is the recording name of US producer and songwriter Tom Shear, active since the late 1990s. His debut album “Contempt” placed him at the front of the electro-industrial and Future Pop scene that took hold on underground dancefloors at the turn of the millennium. Side-Line interviewed Shear about his long career and songwriting process. “Null”, Shear’s tenth album as Assemblage 23, was announced for Metropolis Records and released on 7 November 2025, led by the single “Tolerate”. Shear’s lyrics have long dealt directly with difficult personal subjects, including suicide and depression, a directness that has built him a following that keeps him touring regularly. “Believe (INHALT Remix)”, out 2 October 2026, pairs the “Null” opener with a rework by Matia Simovich (INHALT) ahead of Assemblage 23’s latest run of European dates.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于Assemblage 23单曲《Believe (INHALT Remix)》发布的新闻稿。内容介绍了Tom Shear的第十张专辑《Null》中开场曲被美国制作人Matia Simovich（以INHALT为名）重新混音。Shear形容这个版本一脚踩在80年代中期的舞池上，另一脚坚定地迈向未来。文章还提及了2026年10月的欧洲巡演日期以及《Believe》原曲关于在艰难时世中保持希望的主题。作为electro-industrial和Future Pop领域的资深制作人，Shear自1990年代末活跃至今，歌词长期直接触及自杀和抑郁等个人议题。这次混音将原作与INHALT的制作风格结合，在保持原曲内核的同时进行电子重组。整体内容偏新闻通稿性质，缺乏深入的乐评分析。

items.body: Miss Construction returns with “This Is Crap”, a new EBM and industrial-electro album that pairs eleven new tracks with a reissue of the project’s 2008 debut. Out 27 November 2026 on Out Of Line as a 2CD digipak, it follows “Boys & Ladies”, the sixth single, released 30 September. Disc one holds the eleven new tracks: This Is Crap (Intro) 6666 Heiß Hate Spiel Mit Mir Back Again F.M.P. Boys & Ladies This Is War Bully Du This Is Crap by Miss Construction Disc two reissues “Kunstprodukt,” Miss Construction’s debut album, originally released 28 April 2008 on Fear Section. It adds two archival remixes to the original sixteen tracks: the title track remixed by Gintronic, and “Electro Beast” remixed by Dolls Of Pain. “Boys & Ladies” arrived as an official video through Out Of Line Music’s YouTube channel on 30 September, embedded below. Miss Construction’s road back to ‘This Is Crap’ “Boys & Ladies” caps a run of five singles that marked Miss Construction’s return: “Spiel Mit Mir” in October 2025, “Back Again” in December 2025, then “Heiß,” “Hate” and “F.M.P.” through 2026. “This Is Crap” is available to pre-order now through the Out Of Line shop and on Bandcamp. About Miss Construction Miss Construction began in 2008 as a side project of Chris Pohl, who had fronted Blutengel since 1996. Pohl brought in Gordon Mocznay as co-vocalist, and the pair debuted the project at Wave-Gotik-Treffen in Leipzig that year. Its opening statement was a cover of Terminal Choice’s “Totes Fleisch,” placed on the debut album “Kunstprodukt,” released 28 April 2008 on Fear Section, an Out Of Line sublabel. Pohl and Mocznay followed it with “United Trash – The Z Files” in November 2013. Between full-lengths, Miss Construction contributed remixes to Blutengel and Dance Or Die compilations between 2009 and 2011, including the “Awake The Machines” and “Industrial For The Masses” series, before the project went quiet for twelve years. Pohl revived Miss Construction in 2025. “Spiel Mit Mir” opened the comeback that October, “Back Again” followed in December, and “Heiß,” “Hate,” “F.M.P.” and “Boys & Ladies” continued it through 2026. “This Is Crap” closes that run of singles and gives “Kunstprodukt” its first reissue.

items.body: Corlyx released “The Holy Vampire” on 1 October 2026, the fourth single from “The Crimson Tapes,” the darkwave trio’s next album due in early 2027 on Out Of Line Music. Guitarist and producer Brandon Ashley made the track with singer Caitlin Stokes, who also directed and edited its companion video alongside Sereina Winters. Ashley called the track’s tone deliberate: “It’s also quite camp, which Corlyx is a huge fan of.” He placed it close to 2025’s “Purple Pain,” pairing dancefloor elements with a harder deathrock edge than that album. Corlyx’s ‘The Holy Vampire’ leads to ‘The Crimson Tapes’ “The Holy Vampire” is streaming now and available on Bandcamp. About Corlyx Corlyx call their sound “Death Pop,” a label singer Caitlin Stokes coined for a mix of 1980s post-punk and goth rock. The band started in Los Angeles, releasing its first single, “Starlet,” in February 2016, and now splits its time between the UK and Italy, where Stokes works with guitarist and producer Brandon Ashley and bassist Davide Rocco. Corlyx’s video for “Twist Like An Animal” arrived in 2019. The band announced the album “Blood In The Disco” in 2021 behind the single “Take Off Everything,” then returned in 2024 with “Zombie Kid” ahead of the double album “Purple Pain” the following year. Corlyx has toured Europe, the UK and the US with Lord Of The Lost, Massive Ego, Ashbury Heights, Blutengel and Twin Tribes. “Sweeter Than Blood,” “More Anarchy” and “Your Heart In The Serpent’s Mouth” preceded “The Holy Vampire” as the first three singles from “The Crimson Tapes.”
items._cn_summary: Corlyx 发布了新单曲《The Holy Vampire》，作为即将于2027年初发行的专辑《The Crimson Tapes》的第四首先行曲。乐队自称其风格为"Death Pop"，由主唱 Caitlin Stokes 创造，意指融合80年代后朋克与哥特摇滚的混合体。吉他手兼制作人 Brandon Ashley 强调这首曲子的基调刻意营造出 camp 感，同时加入舞曲元素与比前作更硬核的死亡摇滚边缘。乐队最初在洛杉矶成军，目前已活跃于英国与意大利两地，与多位欧洲暗黑场景代表人物。整体内容为新闻稿性质，缺乏对音乐细节与艺术价值的深入评论，仅作为新单发布的信息通报。

items.body: Danish/UK electronic duo Oui Plastique release the single “For The Cry Of Anguish” on October 16, 2026 through Town and Towers Records. It is the fourth and final single from the project’s second album, “Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It”, due November 27, 2026 on the same Danish label. A Bandcamp page for the single had not gone live at the time of writing. Oui Plastique close the singles campaign for ‘Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It’ “For The Cry Of Anguish” follows three earlier singles from the same album: “Revival” in April 2026, “Linger” on June 12, 2026, and “Spirit” on September 4, 2026. “Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It” is Oui Plastique’s second album, following the 2022 debut “Fraternity of Strangers”. It runs 14 tracks and releases digitally, on CD and on vinyl through Town and Towers Records on November 27, 2026. Oui Plastique set up the song’s premise directly: “For The Cry Of Anguish is a song about seeing something you were never meant to see – and discovering that some things, once witnessed, can never be unseen.“ Oui Plastique previously posted a teaser video for “Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It” to the duo’s YouTube channel, titled “Oui Plastique – ‘Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It’ – Album Teaser”. About Oui Plastique Oui Plastique is the duo of Martin Nyrup (Denmark) and James Thomas (UK). The project grew out of a 2017 collaboration between Nyrup, also one half of the dark wave duo Perpacity, and Thomas, of the band DVL, who together recorded the album “Convergence” that year. In 2018 the pair recorded a three-track covers EP for the UnMute project, a tribute to Mute Records, released on Bandcamp as “UM EP 04” on February 1, 2019. Before the debut album, four of its eventual tracks appeared as standalone digital singles: “Failure” on March 8, 2021, “The Fear” on May 28, 2021, “Crossing Over” on September 24, 2021, and “Wish Yourself Away” on November 26, 2021. The 11-track debut album “Fraternity of Strangers” followed on January 28, 2022, on CD through ScentAir Records. A remastered edition of “Convergence” followed in 2022. In August 2025, the UnMute covers were remastered and reissued across platforms as the EP “UnMute”, featuring the Martin Gore-associated tracks “Compulsion”, “The Bottom Line” and “It Doesn’t Matter Two”, through Town and Towers Records. Nyrup’s other project, Perpacity, released the album “Discordia” in 2023 and the Danish-language single “Lille Flamme” in May 2025. “Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It” arrives on November 27, 2026. It is Oui Plastique’s first full-length through Town and Towers Records, following the 2022 debut on ScentAir Records.
items._cn_summary: 本文为丹麦/英国二人电子组合 Oui Plastique 新单曲及第二张专辑《Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It》的宣传性新闻稿。文章罗列了单曲发行日期、此前三首单曲的时间线、乐队成员构成（Nyrup 同时参与暗潮组合 Perpacity，Thomas 来自乐队 DVL）、首张专辑及翻唱 EP 的发行历史等基础信息。歌曲概念被概括为'目睹不应见之物，一旦目睹便无法忘却'的主题。未涉及任何音乐制作分析、编曲细节、声音设计或对作品艺术价值的评论。乐队归属于 Town and Towers Records 等独立小厂牌，符合暗潮与电子领域定位，但原文缺乏实质性乐评内容。

items.body: Once a song reaches the stage, its authors have to negotiate with a whole new set of circumstances: the room, the volume, the audience, and whatever mood everyone brought through the door. For Brooklyn alternative rock outfit The Amatory Murder, that unpredictability is part of the appeal. Their new live album, We’ve Lost Our Minds: The Amatory Murder Live, is out today, October 2, bringing twelve performances from Brooklyn’s Lucky 13 Saloon to streaming platforms. Drawing on songs from across their catalog, the album documents the heavier, more spontaneous side of a group whose music brings together alternative rock, classic rock, and electronics. The familiar melodies and arrangements remain central, while the live setting gives the material room to change its disposition. For a band that has spent years building its audience through club shows, festivals, and independent touring across the United States, these recordings offer a document of the work done face to face. “There’s something that happens to these songs when we play them live that you can’t completely recreate in the studio,” says Xian Murder. “The energy changes, and sometimes the songs become something different altogether. We wanted to capture that honestly.” Vocalist, songwriter, producer, and founder Xian Murder leads the band alongside bassist Binx Noir and guitarist Jake Haimowitz. Their influences stretch from the expansive rock of Pink Floyd and Muse to Nine Inch Nails, Depeche Mode, The Cult, Joy Division, and David Bowie, a range that helps account for the combination of heavy guitars, electronic detail, and melodic songwriting at the center of their music. Alex Reyes recorded the album at Lucky 13 Saloon, with Dan Kramer handling the mix at Brooklyn’s Skillman Labs and Mark Allen Miller mastering. The release turns that local stage into a meeting point for listeners further afield, giving longtime followers another perspective on the songs and newcomers a way into the band’s live repertoire. We’ve Lost Our Minds is available now on Spotify, Apple Music, and other major streaming platforms. Listen to the album below: The first performance video from the album, “Say Hey (For Doomsday),” offers a visual introduction to the release. Watch below: Later this month, The Amatory Murder return to Lucky 13 Saloon for a Halloween Eve show with Witchforce, Mykey Massacre, and Mannequin Heist. It is a fitting place to pick up where the recording leaves off, with another evening in the room that gave the album its setting. October 30 — Brooklyn, NY — Lucky 13 Saloon, 644 Sackett Street, with Witchforce, Mykey Massacre, and Mannequin Heist. Ages 21+. Doors at 7:30 p.m.; show at 8 p.m. Tickets: $15 in advance, $20 on the day of the show. Tickets here.
